translations.literal: Biography 62, Loyalty and Righteousness 4 ○ Ma Qingxiang, Shang Heng, Shijia Tuoluohui, Yang Dafu, Feng Yandeng, Wugusun Zhongduan, Wugusun Nushen, Pucha Qi, Cai Baer, Wendun Changsun, Wanyan Jiangshan, Bi Zilun, Guo Xiama
translations.idiomatic: Biography 62: Loyalty and Righteousness, Part 4 — Ma Qingxiang; Shang Heng; Shijia Tuoluohui; Yang Dafu; Feng Yandeng; Wugusun Zhongduan; Wugusun Nushen; Pucha Qi; Cai Baer; Wendun Changsun; Wanyan Jiangshan; Bi Zilun; Guo Xiama

sentences.zh: 馬慶祥

translations.literal: Ma Qingxiang
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qingxiang

sentences.zh: 馬慶祥，字瑞甯，本名習禮吉思。

translations.literal: Ma Qingxiang, courtesy name Ruining, original name Xilijisi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qingxiang, whose courtesy name was Ruining and whose original name was Xilijisi,

sentences.zh: 先世自西城入居臨洮狄道，以馬為氏，後徙家淨州天山。

translations.literal: His ancestors entered from the Western Regions and settled at Lintao Didao, taking Ma as their clan name; later the family moved to Tianshan in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had come from the Western Regions and settled in Didao, Lintao, adopting the surname Ma; the family later relocated to Tianshan in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泰和中，試補尚書省譯史。

translations.literal: In the Taihe reign, he passed examination and was appointed translator-scribe in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he qualified and was appointed a translator-scribe in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大安初，衛王始通問大元，選使副，上曰：「習禮吉思智辯通六國語，往必無辱也。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an, the Prince of Wei first opened communications with the Great Yuan; when envoys were chosen, the emperor said: "Xilijisi is clever and eloquent and knows the languages of six states—he will surely go without disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Da'an era, when the Prince of Wei first sent envoys to the Great Yuan, the court had to choose a deputy envoy. The emperor said, "Xilijisi is clever, eloquent, and fluent in the languages of six states—he will certainly acquit himself without shame."

sentences.zh: 使還，授開封府判官。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed administrative aide of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the embassy returned, he was appointed administrative aide of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 內城之役充應辦使，不擾而事集。

translations.literal: During the inner-city campaign he served as provisioning commissioner and accomplished the tasks without disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign to secure the inner city he served as provisioning commissioner, completing the work without troubling the populace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大元兵出陝右，朝廷命完顏仲元為鳳翔元帥，舉慶祥為副，上曰：「此朕志也，且築城有勞。」

translations.literal: Before long, Great Yuan troops emerged from the right of Shaanxi; the court appointed Wanyan Zhongyuan commander of Fengxiang and nominated Qingxiang as his deputy; the emperor said: "This accords with my wish, and moreover he has labored at wall-building."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuan forces appeared from western Shaanxi. The court appointed Wanyan Zhongyuan military commander of Fengxiang and nominated Qingxiang as his deputy. The emperor said, "This is what I intend, and he has already earned merit in building the city's defenses."

sentences.zh: 即拜鳳翔府路兵馬都總管判官。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed administrative aide under the overall commander of Fengxiang Circuit's military forces.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxiang was immediately confirmed as administrative aide to the overall commander of military forces for Fengxiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元光元年冬十一月，聞大將萌古不花將攻鳳翔，行省檄慶祥與治中胥謙分道清野。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter in the first year of Yuanguang, hearing that the grand general Mengubuhua would attack Fengxiang, the Branch Secretariat ordered Qingxiang and Administrative Aide Xu Qian to clear the countryside by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, the first year of Yuanguang, word came that the grand general Mengubuhua would attack Fengxiang. The Branch Secretariat ordered Qingxiang and Xu Qian, the circuit administrative aide, to clear the countryside along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 將行，命畫工肖其貌，付其家人。

translations.literal: About to depart, he had a painter take his likeness and gave it to his family.
translations.idiomatic: Before setting out, he had a painter take his likeness and gave the portrait to his family.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「君方壯，何乃為此不祥？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Sir, you are still in your prime—why do something so ill-omened?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "You are still in your prime—why do something so ominous?"

sentences.zh: 慶祥曰：「非汝所知也。」

translations.literal: Qingxiang said: "That is not for you to understand."
translations.idiomatic: Qingxiang replied, "That is not something you would understand."

sentences.zh: 明日遂行。

translations.literal: The next day he set out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he departed.

sentences.zh: 遇先鋒于澮水，戰不利。

translations.literal: He met the vanguard at the Hui River and the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: Near the Hui River he met the enemy vanguard and fared poorly in the fight.

sentences.zh: 且行且戰，將及城，會大兵邀其歸路，度不能脫，令其騎曰：「吾屬荷國厚恩，竭力效死，乃其職也。」

translations.literal: Fighting as he went, he drew near the city when main forces blocked his retreat; seeing he could not escape, he told his horsemen: "We have received the state's deep favor—exerting ourselves unto death is our duty."
translations.idiomatic: Fighting as he withdrew, he was nearing the city when the main enemy army cut off his line of retreat. Realizing he could not break free, he told his horsemen, "We owe the state a deep debt of gratitude—to give our utmost even unto death is our duty."

sentences.zh: 諸騎皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: All the horsemen said: "Aye."
translations.idiomatic: Every rider answered, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 人殊死戰，良久矢盡。

translations.literal: The men fought to the death; after a long time their arrows were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They fought with desperate fury until at last their arrows ran out.

sentences.zh: 大兵圍數匝，欲降之，軍擁以行，語言往復，竟不屈而死，年四十有六。

translations.literal: The main army surrounded them in several rings and wished to accept their surrender; the troops seized him and escorted him along, words went back and forth, yet in the end he would not submit and died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The main army closed round them in ring after ring and tried to accept their surrender. Soldiers seized Qingxiang and hustled him along; argument followed argument, but he would not yield and died—aged forty-six.

sentences.zh: 元帥郭仲元輿其屍以歸，葬鳳翔普門寺之東。

translations.literal: Commander Guo Zhongyuan carried his body back and buried him east of Pumen Temple in Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Guo Zhongyuan bore his body back for burial east of Pumen Temple in Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔贈輔國上將軍、恆州刺史，諡忠湣。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict posthumously awarded him Assistant General for Assisting the State and Prefect of Hengzhou, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Assistant General for Assisting the State and Prefect of Hengzhou, with the posthumous name Zhongmin ("Loyal and Grieving").

sentences.zh: 胥謙及其子嗣亨亦不屈死，謙贈輔國上將軍、彰化軍節度使，嗣亨贈威遠將軍、鳳翔府判官。

translations.literal: Xu Qian and his son Sihou also died without submitting; Qian was posthumously awarded Assistant General for Assisting the State and military commissioner of Zhanghua Army; Sihou was posthumously awarded General for Distant Prestige and administrative aide of Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian and his son Sihou likewise refused to submit and died. Qian was posthumously made Assistant General for Assisting the State and commissioner of the Zhanghua army; Sihou was posthumously made General for Distant Prestige and administrative aide of Fengxiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楨州金勝堡提控僕散胡沙亦死，贈銀青榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: Husca of the Pusan clan, troop commander at Jinsheng Fort in Zhen Prefecture, also died and was posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Silver-Green Girdle of Glory and Honor.
translations.idiomatic: Husca of the Pusan clan, troop commander at Jinsheng Fort in Zhen Prefecture, also died and was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master of the Silver-Green Girdle of Glory and Honor.

sentences.zh: 正大二年，哀宗詔褒死節士，若馬習禮吉思、王清、田榮、李貴、王斌、馮萬奴、張德威、高行中、程濟、姬芃、張山等十有三人，為立褒忠廟，仍錄其孤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengda, Emperor Aizong issued an edict to honor men who died for principle, such as Ma Xilijisi, Wang Qing, Tian Rong, Li Gui, Wang Bin, Feng Wannu, Zhang Dewei, Gao Xingzhong, Cheng Ji, Ji Peng, Zhang Shan, and thirteen others in all, erecting a Temple to Honor Loyalty and still enrolling their orphans.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 2, Emperor Aizong issued an edict to honor men who had died steadfast in loyalty—including Ma Xilijisi, Wang Qing, Tian Rong, Li Gui, Wang Bin, Feng Wannu, Zhang Dewei, Gao Xingzhong, Cheng Ji, Ji Peng, Zhang Shan, and thirteen others in all—by founding a Temple to Honor Loyalty and enrolling their surviving dependents.

sentences.zh: 二人者逸其名，餘亦無所考。

translations.literal: Two men's names are lost; the rest also cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Two of the men are known only without surviving names; the rest cannot be identified with certainty either.

sentences.zh: 商衡

translations.literal: Shang Heng
translations.idiomatic: Shang Heng

sentences.zh: 商衡，字平叔，曹州人。

translations.literal: Shang Heng, courtesy name Pingshu, was a native of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Heng, whose courtesy name was Pingshu, was a native of Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年，特恩第一人，授鄜州洛郊主簿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhi'ning he ranked first in the special grace examination and was appointed recorder of Luojiao in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhi'ning he ranked first in the special grace examination and was appointed recorder of Luojiao in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以廉能換郿縣，尋辟威戎令。

translations.literal: For integrity and ability he was transferred to Mei County, and soon afterward was invited to serve as magistrate of Weirong.
translations.idiomatic: For integrity and ability he was transferred to Mei County, and soon afterward was invited to serve as magistrate of Weirong.

sentences.zh: 興定三年，歲饑，民無所於糴，衡白行省，得開倉賑貸，全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xingding there was famine and the people had nowhere to buy grain. Heng reported to the branch secretariat and obtained permission to open the granaries for relief loans, saving a great many lives.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 3 famine struck and the people had nowhere to buy grain. Heng reported to the branch secretariat, obtained permission to open the granaries for relief loans, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 後因地震城圮，夏人乘釁入侵，衡率蕃部土豪守禦應敵，保以無虞。

translations.literal: Later, because an earthquake destroyed the city walls, the Xia seized the opportunity to invade. Heng led tribal chiefs and local magnates in defense against the enemy and kept the place secure.
translations.idiomatic: Later an earthquake destroyed the city walls, and the Xia seized the opportunity to invade. Heng led tribal chiefs and local magnates in defense and kept the prefecture secure.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，縣人為立生祠。

translations.literal: When his term ended the county people erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended the county people erected a living shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 再辟原武令。

translations.literal: He was again invited to serve as magistrate of Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was again invited to serve as magistrate of Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為尚書省令史，轉戶部主事，兩月拜監察禦史。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the Secretariat as a clerk, was transferred to principal official of the Ministry of Revenue, and after two months was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered the Secretariat as a clerk, was transferred to principal official of the Ministry of Revenue, and after two months was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 哀宗姨郕國夫人不時出入宮闈，干預政事，聲跡甚惡。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong's aunt the Lady of Guo State came in and out of the inner palace at will, intervened in government, and her reputation and conduct were very foul.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong's aunt, the Lady of Guo State, came and went through the inner palace at will, meddled in government affairs, and enjoyed a thoroughly unsavory reputation.

sentences.zh: 衡上章極言，自是郕國被召乃敢進見。

translations.literal: Heng submitted memorials with extreme forthrightness; from then on the Lady of Guo dared enter audience only when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Heng memorialized the throne in the strongest terms, and thereafter the Lady of Guo ventured to appear before the emperor only when formally summoned.

sentences.zh: 內族慶山奴將兵守盱眙，與李全戰敗，朝廷置而不問。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Qingshanu commanded troops defending Xuyi and was defeated by Li Quan; the court ignored it.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Qingshanu commanded the garrison at Xuyi and was defeated by Li Quan, yet the court took no action.

sentences.zh: 衡上言：「自古敗軍之將必正典刑，不爾則無以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Heng submitted: "From antiquity generals who lost battles must face regular penal law; otherwise there is no way to answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Heng memorialized: "Throughout history, generals who lost their armies were punished according to law; otherwise the court could not answer to the realm."

sentences.zh: 詔降慶山奴為定國軍節度使。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Qingshanu to military commissioner of the Dingguo army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Qingshanu to military commissioner of the Dingguo army.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎權尚書曹溫之女在掖庭，親舊干預權利，其家人填委諸司，貪墨彰露。

translations.literal: The daughter of Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Minister Cao Wen was in the inner palace; relatives and friends interfered in power and profit; her household thronged the various offices; greed and corruption stood revealed.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Cao Wen, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting chief minister, held a post in the inner palace. Her kin and associates interfered in office and profit, and her household agents clogged the bureaucracies while corruption was brazenly exposed.

sentences.zh: 台臣無敢言者，衡歷數其罪。

translations.literal: Censorate officials dared not speak; Heng enumerated her crimes one by one.
translations.idiomatic: No censor dared speak up; Heng itemized her offenses in full.

sentences.zh: 詔罷溫戶部，改太后府衛尉。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Wen from Revenue and transferred him to Grand Guard of the Dowager's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Wen from the Ministry of Revenue and appointed him grand guard of the empress dowager's establishment.

sentences.zh: 再上章言：「溫果可罪，當貶逐，無罪則臣為妄言，豈有是非不別而兩可之理。」

translations.literal: He submitted again: "If Wen is truly guilty he should be demoted and expelled; if not, then your servant has spoken falsely—how can there be reason that does not distinguish right from wrong yet has it both ways?"
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "If Wen is guilty, he should be demoted and banished; if not, then I have spoken falsely. There can be no principle that refuses to distinguish right from wrong yet satisfies both sides."

sentences.zh: 哀宗為之動容，乃出溫為汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong was moved and sent Wen out as defense commissioner of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Emperor Aizong transferred Wen to serve as defense commissioner of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為右司都事，改同知河平軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he became director of the right office, then was changed to acting co-administrator of the Heiping Army command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became director of the right office, then was changed to acting co-administrator of the Heiping Army command.

sentences.zh: 未赴，改樞密院經歷官，遙領昌武軍同知節度使事。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was changed to secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and remotely held the post of acting co-administrator of the Changwu Army command.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post he was changed to secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and remotely held the post of acting co-administrator of the Changwu Army command.

sentences.zh: 丞相完顏賽不領陝西行省，奏衡為左右司員外郎，密院表留，有旨：「行省地重，急於得人，可從丞相奏。」

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Wanyan Saibu held the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and memorialized to appoint Heng as outer director of the left and right offices. The Bureau tabled a request to retain him, but an edict said: "The branch secretariat post is weighty and urgent need of capable men—grant the chief councillor's memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Wanyan Saibu held the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and memorialized to appoint Heng as outer director of the left and right offices. The Bureau tabled a request to retain him, but an edict said: "The branch secretariat post is weighty and urgently needs capable men—grant the chief councillor's memorial."

sentences.zh: 明年，召遷，行省再奏留之。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to return to the capital, but the branch secretariat again memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned to return to the capital, but the branch secretariat again memorialized to retain him.

sentences.zh: 正大八年，以母喪還京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengda he returned to the capital on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 8 he returned to the capital on his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 十月，起複為秦藍總帥府經歷官。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was recalled from mourning to serve as secretary of the Qin-Lan commander-in-chief's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was recalled from mourning to serve as secretary of the Qin-Lan commander-in-chief's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 天興元年二月，關陝行省徒單兀典等敗於鐵嶺，衡未知諸帥存歿，招集潰軍以須其至。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tianxing, Tushan Wudian of the Guan-Shaan Branch Secretariat and others were defeated at Tieling. Heng did not know whether the commanders were alive or dead and gathered scattered troops to await their arrival.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianxing 1, Tushan Wudian of the Guan-Shaan Branch Secretariat and others were defeated at Tieling. Heng did not know whether the commanders were alive or dead and gathered scattered troops to await their arrival.

sentences.zh: 遂為兵士所得，欲降之，不為屈。

translations.literal: He was then seized by soldiers who wished to make him surrender, but he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He was then seized by soldiers who wished to make him surrender, but he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 監至長水縣東嶽祠前，誘之使招洛陽，衡曰：「我洛陽識何人，為汝招之耶？」

translations.literal: Under guard he was brought before the Eastern Peak shrine in Changshui County. They tried to induce him to summon Luoyang to surrender. Heng said: "Whom do I know in Luoyang that I should summon it for you?"
translations.idiomatic: Under guard he was brought before the Eastern Peak shrine in Changshui County. They tried to induce him to summon Luoyang to surrender. Heng said: "Whom do I know in Luoyang that I should summon it for you?"

sentences.zh: 兵知不可誘，欲捽其巾。

translations.literal: The soldiers knew he could not be induced and tried to snatch off his headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers knew he could not be induced and tried to snatch off his headcloth.

sentences.zh: 衡瞋目大呼曰：「汝欲脅從我耶？」

translations.literal: Heng glared and shouted: "Do you wish to coerce me into following you?"
translations.idiomatic: Heng glared and shouted: "Do you wish to coerce me into following you?"

sentences.zh: 終不肯降，望闕瞻拜曰：「主將無狀，亡兵失利。

translations.literal: He steadfastly refused to surrender. Facing the palace he bowed and said: "The chief commanders behaved disgracefully and the scattered army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused to surrender. Facing the palace he bowed and said: "The chief commanders behaved disgracefully and the scattered army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 臣子罪責，亦無所逃，但以一死報國耳。」

translations.literal: A subject's guilt cannot be escaped; I can only repay the state with death."
translations.idiomatic: A subject's guilt cannot be escaped; I can only repay the state with death."

sentences.zh: 遂引佩刀自剄，年四十有六。

translations.literal: He then drew his belt dagger and cut his own throat. He was forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew his belt dagger and cut his own throat. He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 正大初，河間許古詣闕拜章，言：「八座率非其材，省寺小臣有可任宰相者，不大升黜之則無以致中興。」

translations.literal: Early in Zhengda, Xu Gu of Hejian came to the capital and submitted a memorial saying: "The eight chief ministers are mostly unfit; among officials of ministries and directorates there are men fit to serve as chief minister—without great promotions and demotions the state cannot achieve restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengda era, Xu Gu of Hejian presented himself at court and submitted a memorial: "The eight chief ministers are for the most part unfit. Among the junior officials of the ministries and directorates there are men fit to serve as chief minister—but without major promotions and demotions there will be no path to restoration."

sentences.zh: 章奏，詔古赴都堂，問孰為可相者，古以衡對，則衡之材可知矣。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, an edict summoned Gu to the chief council hall and asked who could serve as chief minister; Gu answered with Heng, whereby Heng's talent may be known.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was received, the emperor ordered Gu to the chief council hall and asked whom he would recommend as chief minister. Gu named Heng—and from that one may gauge how capable Heng was thought to be.

sentences.zh: 朮甲脫魯灰

translations.literal: Shijia Tuoluohui
translations.idiomatic: Shijia Tuoluohui

sentences.zh: 朮甲脫魯灰，上京人，世為北京路部長。

translations.literal: Shijia Tuoluohui, a native of Shangjing, for generations hereditary chief of a tribe in Beijing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shijia Tuoluohui was a native of Shangjing whose family had for generations served as hereditary tribal chiefs in Beijing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 其先有開國功，授北京路宋阿答阿猛安，脫魯灰自幼襲爵。

translations.literal: His forebear rendered founding merit and was granted the meng'an post of Song'ada'a in Beijing Circuit; Tuoluohui inherited the title from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor had rendered founding service and been granted the meng'an post of Song'ada'a in Beijing Circuit; Tuoluohui inherited the title from childhood.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，宣宗遷汴，率本部兵赴中都扈從，上喜，特授御前馬步軍都總領。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, he led his tribal troops to Zhongdu to escort the emperor; the emperor was pleased and specially appointed him overall commander of the imperial horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2, when Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Tuoluohui led his tribal forces to Zhongdu to escort the emperor. Delighted, the emperor specially appointed him overall commander of the imperial horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 宋人略南鄙，命同簽樞密院事時全將大軍南伐，脫魯灰率本部屢摧宋兵破城寨，以功遙授昌武軍節度使、元帥右都監、行蔡、息等路元帥府事。

translations.literal: When Song forces raided the southern marches, the court ordered Shi Quan, Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to lead a great army south; Tuoluohui led his tribe repeatedly crushing Song troops and capturing forts and stockades; for merit he was remotely appointed military commissioner of Changwu Army, right overseer of the commander-in-chief, and acting commander of the military headquarters for Cai, Xi, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces raided the southern frontier, the court ordered Shi Quan, associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to lead a major campaign south. Tuoluohui led his tribal forces in repeated victories over Song armies, capturing forts and stockades. For these services he was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Changwu army, right overseer under the commander-in-chief, and acting head of the military headquarters for Cai, Xi, and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 既而，宋人有因畜牧越境者，邏卒擒之，法當械送朝廷，脫魯灰曰：「國家自遷都以來，境土日蹙，民力凋耗，幸邊無事，人稍得息。

translations.literal: Later, when Song men crossed the border while grazing livestock, border patrols seized them; by law they should be sent in shackles to the court; Tuoluohui said: "Since the state moved its capital, territory has daily shrunk and the people's strength has withered; fortunately the border is quiet and people have slightly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Song herdsmen crossed the border while grazing livestock, border patrols seized them. By law they should have been sent in shackles to the capital. Tuoluohui said, "Since the court moved the capital, our territory has steadily shrunk and the people have been exhausted. We are fortunate that the frontier has been quiet and the populace has barely had a chance to breathe.

sentences.zh: 若戮此曹，則邊釁複生，兵連禍結矣。

translations.literal: If we kill these men, border incidents will arise again and war will link with calamity unending.
translations.idiomatic: If we execute these men, border incidents will flare up again and war will bring unending disaster.

sentences.zh: 不如釋之，以絕兵端。」

translations.literal: Better to release them and cut off the cause of war."
translations.idiomatic: Better to release them and remove the cause of war."

sentences.zh: 哀宗即位，授鎮南軍節度使、蔡州管內觀察使、行戶、工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong ascended the throne, Tuoluohui was appointed military commissioner of the Zhennan Army, observer of Caizhou, and acting Minister of Revenue and Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong took the throne, Tuoluohui was appointed military commissioner of the Zhennan Army, observer of Caizhou, and acting Minister of Revenue and Works.

sentences.zh: 時大元兵入陝西。

translations.literal: At that time the Great Yuan army entered Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Great Yuan army entered Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 乃上章曰：「宋人與我為仇敵，頃以力屈自保，非其本心。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "The Song are our enemies. Recently they have submitted only because force compelled them—it is not their true intent.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "The Song are our enemies. They have submitted only because force compelled them—it is not their true intent.

sentences.zh: 今陝西被兵，河南出師，轉戰連年不絕，兵死於陣，民疲於役，國力竭矣。

translations.literal: Now Shaanxi is under attack and Henan has sent armies forth. Fighting has continued year after year without cease. Soldiers die in battle and the people are worn out by labor service. The state's strength is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shaanxi is under attack and Henan has sent armies forth. Fighting has continued year after year without cease. Soldiers die in battle, the people are worn out by labor service, and the state's strength is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 壽、泗一帶南接盱、楚，紅襖賊李全巢穴也。

translations.literal: The Shou and Si region borders Xuyi and Chu to the south—the lair of Li Quan, chief of the Red-Jacket rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Shou and Si region borders Xuyi and Chu to the south—the lair of Li Quan, leader of the Red-Jacket rebels.

sentences.zh: 萬一宋人諜知，與全乘虛而入，腹背受敵，非計之得者也。

translations.literal: If by chance the Song learn of our situation and join with Quan to strike while we are exposed, we will be attacked front and rear—this is no prudent plan.
translations.idiomatic: If the Song learn of our situation and join with Quan to strike while we are exposed, we will be attacked front and rear—this is no prudent plan.

sentences.zh: 臣已令所部沿邊警斥，以備非常。

translations.literal: Your servant has already ordered his subordinates along the border to keep watch and guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has already ordered his subordinates along the border to keep watch and guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 宜敕壽、泗帥臣謹斥候，嚴烽燧，常若敵至，此兵法所謂'無恃其不來，特吾有以待之'之道也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should command the commanders of Shou and Si to maintain scouts diligently, keep beacon fires strict, and always act as though the enemy were at hand—this is what military doctrine calls the principle of 'Do not rely on the enemy not coming; rely on your own readiness to meet him.'"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should command the commanders of Shou and Si to maintain scouts diligently, keep beacon fires strict, and always act as though the enemy were at hand—this is what military doctrine calls the principle of 'Do not rely on the enemy not coming; rely on your own readiness to meet him.'"

sentences.zh: 上是而行之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 正大二年秋，傳言宋人將入侵，農司令民先期刈禾，脫魯灰曰：「夫民所恃以仰事俯育及供億國家者，秋成而已。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Zhengda, rumor said Song would invade; the Agriculture Office ordered the people to reap early; Tuoluohui said: "What the people rely on to support their superiors, nurture their inferiors, and supply the state is only the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Zhengda 2, rumor spread that the Song would invade. The Agriculture Office ordered the people to reap their grain early. Tuoluohui said, "The people depend on the autumn harvest alone to support their elders, raise their children, and supply the state.

sentences.zh: 今使秋無所獲，國何以仰，民何以給？」

translations.literal: Now if autumn yields nothing, how will the state be supplied, how will the people be fed?"
translations.idiomatic: If we leave them nothing from the autumn, how will the state be fed, and how will the people survive?"

sentences.zh: 遂遣軍巡邏，聽民待熟而刈，宋人卒不入寇。

translations.literal: He then sent troops to patrol and allowed the people to wait until ripe before reaping; the Song in the end did not invade.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent troops to patrol the frontier and allowed the people to wait until the grain was ripe before reaping. In the end the Song did not invade.

sentences.zh: 諜者又報光州汪太尉將以八月發兵來取真陽，議者請籍丁男以備，脫魯灰曰：「汪太尉恇怯人耳，寧敢為此？

translations.literal: Spies again reported that Grand Marshal Wang of Guang Prefecture would in the eighth month raise troops to take Zhenyang; councillors asked to register able-bodied men for defense; Tuoluohui said: "Grand Marshal Wang is a timid man—how would he dare do this?
translations.idiomatic: Spies again reported that the Grand Marshal Wang of Guang Prefecture would raise troops in the eighth month to seize Zhenyang. Councillors proposed registering able-bodied men for defense. Tuoluohui said, "Grand Marshal Wang is a timid man—how would he dare attempt such a thing?

sentences.zh: 必奸人聲言來寇，欲使吾民廢務也，不可信。」

translations.literal: It must be villains spreading word of invasion to make our people abandon their work—do not believe it."
translations.idiomatic: This must be troublemakers spreading rumors of invasion to make our people abandon their work. It is not to be believed."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: In time it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: In time events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 叛人焦風子者，沿河南北屢為反復，朝廷授以提控之職，令將三千人戍遂平。

translations.literal: The rebel Jiao Fengzi, who along the Yellow River north and south had repeatedly shifted sides, was granted the post of troop commander and ordered to lead three thousand men to garrison Suiping.
translations.idiomatic: The turncoat Jiao Fengzi had repeatedly switched allegiance along both banks of the Yellow River. The court appointed him troop commander and ordered him to lead three thousand men to garrison Suiping.

sentences.zh: 四年春，風子謀率其眾入宋，脫魯灰策之，以兵數千伏鄱陽道，賊果夜出此途，伏發殪之。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year, Fengzi plotted to lead his followers into Song; Tuoluohui anticipated it, placed several thousand troops in ambush on the Poyang road; the bandits indeed came out by night on this route and the ambush rose and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, Fengzi plotted to lead his followers over to the Song. Tuoluohui anticipated the move and stationed several thousand troops in ambush on the Poyang road. The rebels did indeed march out by night along that route, and the ambush rose and annihilated them.

sentences.zh: 七年，大元兵攻藍關，至八渡倉退。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Great Yuan troops attacked Languan and withdrew at Badu Granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Yuan forces attacked Languan and withdrew after reaching Badu Granary.

sentences.zh: 舉朝皆賀，以為無事。

translations.literal: The whole court congratulated one another, thinking there was no further trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court congratulated itself, believing the danger had passed.

sentences.zh: 脫魯灰獨言曰：「潼關險隘，兵精足用。

translations.literal: Tuoluohui alone said: "Tong Pass is perilous and narrow, with elite troops sufficient for use.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoluohui alone warned, "Tong Pass is perilous and narrow, and its garrison is strong enough for defense.

sentences.zh: 然商、洛以南瀕於宋境，大山重複，宋人不知守，國家亦不能逾宋境屯戍。

translations.literal: Yet south of Shang and Luo it borders Song territory, with great mountains in layers; the Song do not know to defend it, and our state also cannot station garrisons beyond Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet south of Shang and Luo the land borders Song territory, where great mountains rise in layers. The Song do not know to defend it, and we cannot post garrisons beyond the Song frontier either.

sentences.zh: 大兵若由散關入興元，下金、房，繞出襄、漢，北入鄧鄙，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: If the main army enters Xingyuan by San Pass, descends on Jin and Fang, circles out through Xiang and Han, and enters north into Deng and the outskirts, then the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If the main army enters Xingyuan through San Pass, descends on Jin and Fang, circles out through Xiang and Han, and drives north into Deng and its hinterland, then all will be lost.

sentences.zh: 宜與宋人釋怨，諭以輔車之勢，脣亡齒寒，彼必見從。

translations.literal: We should release grievances with the Song and instruct them in the chariot-and-sidecar relation—when the lips perish the teeth grow cold—and they will surely comply.
translations.idiomatic: We should settle our grievances with the Song and explain that we are like the chariot and its side rails—when the lips perish the teeth grow cold—and they will surely agree.

sentences.zh: 據其險要以備，不然必敗。」

translations.literal: Hold its strategic passes in defense; otherwise we are sure to be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: We must hold its strategic passes in defense—or we are certain to be defeated."

sentences.zh: 是秋，必授小關子元帥，屯商州大吉口。

translations.literal: That autumn, Bi Shou was appointed commander of Xiaoguanzi and encamped at Dajikou in Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, Bi Shou was appointed commander of Xiaoguanzi and encamped at Dajikou in Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九年春，從行省參政徒單吾典將潼關兵入援，至商山遇雪，大兵邀擊之，士卒饑凍，不能戰而潰。

translations.literal: In spring of the ninth year, following Branch Secretariat Administrator Tushan Wudian, he led Tong Pass troops to reinforce; reaching Shangshan they met snow; the main army intercepted them; soldiers hungered and froze, could not fight, and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he followed Tushan Wudian, administrator of the Branch Secretariat, leading Tong Pass troops to reinforce the capital. At Shangshan they were caught in snow; the main army intercepted them; the men, starving and freezing, could not fight and broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 脫魯灰被執不屈，拔佩刀自殺。

translations.literal: Tuoluohui was seized and would not submit; he drew his belt dagger and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoluohui was captured but refused to submit; he drew his belt dagger and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 楊達夫

translations.literal: Yang Dafu
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dafu

sentences.zh: 楊達夫，字晉卿，耀州三原人。

translations.literal: Yang Dafu, courtesy name Jinqing, was a native of Sanyuan in Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dafu, whose courtesy name was Jinqing, was a native of Sanyuan in Yao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Taihe 3.

sentences.zh: 有才幹，所至可紀。

translations.literal: He had ability; wherever he went there were deeds worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: He was capable, and wherever he served he left accomplishments worth recording.

sentences.zh: 召補省掾，草奏章，坐字誤，降平涼府判官。

translations.literal: Summoned to fill a provincial clerk post, he drafted memorials; for a character error he was demoted to administrative aide of Pingliang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as a provincial clerk and drafted memorials, but a character error in his writing led to his demotion to administrative aide of Pingliang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗主鄠縣簿，事一從簡，吏民樂之。

translations.literal: He once served as registrar of Hu County; affairs were kept simple throughout and officials and people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as registrar of Hu County, keeping affairs simple throughout, to the delight of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 達夫亦愛其山水之勝，因家焉。

translations.literal: Dafu also loved the excellence of its mountains and waters and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu also fell in love with the beauty of its landscape and made his home there.

sentences.zh: 日以詩酒自娛，了無宦情。

translations.literal: Day by day he amused himself with poetry and wine, with no ambition for office whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: He passed his days in poetry and wine, with no appetite for official career at all.

sentences.zh: 會有詔徙民東入關，達夫與眾行，及韶，避兵於州北之橫嶺，為遊騎所執，將褫衣害之。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered the people moved east into the passes, Dafu went with the multitude; reaching Shao, he avoided troops at Hengling north of the prefecture, was seized by roaming horsemen, and they were about to strip his clothes and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the populace relocated east into the passes, Dafu traveled with the crowd. At Shao he took refuge from fighting at Hengling north of the prefecture, but roaming horsemen seized him and were about to strip him and kill him.

sentences.zh: 達夫挺然直立馬首，略無所懼。

translations.literal: Dafu stood erect before the horse's head, showing no fear at all.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu stood bolt upright before the horsemen, showing not the slightest fear.

sentences.zh: 稍侵辱之，即大言曰：「我金國臣子，即為汝所執，不過一死，忍裸袒以黷天日耶！」

translations.literal: When they insulted him somewhat, he cried out: "I am a subject of the Jin state; though seized by you, it is only death—how could I bear to strip bare and profane heaven's light!"
translations.idiomatic: When they insulted him further, he cried out, "I am a subject of the Jin state! Even seized by you, I face no more than death—would you have me strip bare and profane heaven's light?"

sentences.zh: 遂見殺。

translations.literal: He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then killed.

sentences.zh: 兩山潛伏之民竊觀之者，皆相告曰：「若此好官，異日祠之，當作我橫嶺之神。」

translations.literal: The people hiding on both hills who secretly watched all told one another: "Such a good official—when we enshrine him another day, he should become the god of our Hengling."
translations.idiomatic: The people hiding on the hillsides who had watched in secret told one another, "An official like this—when we enshrine him one day, he should become the god of our Hengling."

sentences.zh: 馮延登

translations.literal: Feng Yandeng
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yandeng

sentences.zh: 馮延登，字子俊，吉州吉鄉人。

translations.literal: Feng Yandeng, courtesy name Zijun, was a native of Jixiang in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yandeng, whose courtesy name was Zijun, was a native of Jixiang in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世業醫。

translations.literal: His family profession was medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His family had practiced medicine for generations.

sentences.zh: 延登幼穎悟，既長，事舉業，承安二年登詞賦進士第。

translations.literal: Yandeng was clever as a child; when grown he pursued the examination curriculum; in the second year of Chengan he passed the jinshi in the rhapsody category.
translations.idiomatic: Yandeng was precocious as a boy. When he grew up he pursued the civil-service examinations and in Chengan 2 received his jinshi degree in the rhapsody category.

sentences.zh: 調臨真簿、德順州軍事判官。

translations.literal: He was assigned as registrar of Linzhen and military administrative aide of Deshun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed registrar of Linzhen and military administrative aide of Deshun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，轉甯邊令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe, he was transferred to magistrate of Ningbian.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 he was transferred to magistrate of Ningbian.

sentences.zh: 大安元年秋七月，霜害稼，民艱於食，延登發粟賑貸，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the first year of Da'an, frost harmed the crops and the people had difficulty in food; Yandeng distributed grain for relief and lending, saving very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Da'an 1, frost ruined the crops and the people faced famine. Yandeng distributed grain for relief and loans, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，補尚書省令史，尋授河中府判官、兼行尚書省左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, he was appointed clerk of the Ministry of Revenue; soon after he was made administrative aide of Hezhong Prefecture and concurrent outer vice-director of the left and right departments of the acting Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and soon afterward was made administrative aide of Hezhong Prefecture while also serving as outer vice-director of the left and right departments of the acting Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 興定五年，入為國史院編修官，改太常博士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding, he entered service as compiler in the National History Institute and was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 5 he entered the National History Institute as a compiler and was transferred to serve as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元光二年，知登聞鼓院，兼翰林修撰，奉使夏國，就充接送伴使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanguang, he was director of the Petition Drum Court and concurrent Hanlin reviser; on embassy to Xia he was appointed receiving and escorting companion envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanguang he directed the Petition Drum Court while also serving as Hanlin reviser. On an embassy to Xia he was appointed receiving and escorting companion envoy.

sentences.zh: 正大七年十二月，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Zhengda, he was promoted to libationer of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhengda 7 he was promoted to libationer of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 假翰林學士承旨，充國信使。

translations.literal: Acting as Hanlin academician recipient of edicts, he served as credentialed envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as Hanlin academician recipient of edicts, he served as credentialed envoy to the Yuan court.

sentences.zh: 以八年春奉國書朝見於虢縣禦營。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he presented the state letter and had audience at the imperial camp in Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he presented the state letter and had audience at the imperial camp in Guo County.

sentences.zh: 有旨問：「汝識鳳翔帥否？」

translations.literal: An order asked: "Do you know the commander of Fengxiang?"
translations.idiomatic: He was asked by imperial order, "Do you know the commander of Fengxiang?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「識之。」

translations.literal: He answered: "I know him."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I do."

sentences.zh: 又問：「何如人？」

translations.literal: He was asked again: "What sort of man is he?"
translations.idiomatic: He was asked again, "What sort of man is he?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「敏於事者也。」

translations.literal: He said: "He is quick in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "He is quick and capable in affairs."

sentences.zh: 又問：「汝能招之使降即貰汝死，不則殺汝矣。」

translations.literal: He was asked again: "If you can summon him to surrender, your death will be pardoned; otherwise you will be killed."
translations.idiomatic: He was asked again, "If you can induce him to surrender, your life will be spared; otherwise you will be killed."

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣奉書請和，招降豈使職乎。

translations.literal: He said: "Your servant bears a letter seeking peace—how is inducing surrender an envoy's duty?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I bear a letter seeking peace—how would inducing surrender be an envoy's duty?

sentences.zh: 招降亦死，還朝亦死，不若今日即死為愈也。」

translations.literal: To induce surrender is also death, to return to court is also death—better to die today at once."
translations.idiomatic: Inducing surrender means death, and returning to court means death as well—better to die here today."

sentences.zh: 明日，複問：「汝曾思之不？」

translations.literal: The next day he was asked again: "Have you thought it over?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was asked again, "Have you reconsidered?"

sentences.zh: 對如前，問至再三，執義不回。

translations.literal: He answered as before; questioned again and again, he held to principle and would not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: He answered as before. Questioned again and again, he held to his principles and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 又明日，乃喻旨雲：「汝罪應死，但古無殺使者理，汝愛汝須髯猶汝命也。」

translations.literal: The day after again, he was instructed: "Your crime deserves death, but antiquity holds no precedent for killing envoys—cherish your beard as you cherish your life."
translations.idiomatic: On the following day he was told the meaning of his reprieve: "Your offense deserves death, yet antiquity holds that envoys must not be killed. Cherish your beard as you cherish your own life."

sentences.zh: 叱左右以刀截去之，延登岸然不動，乃監之豐州。

translations.literal: He rebuked attendants to cut it off with a knife; Yandeng remained stern and unmoved; he was then detained at Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to cut it off with a knife. Yandeng remained stern and unmoved, and was then detained at Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年後放還，哀宗撫慰久之，複以為祭酒，曆禮、吏二部侍郎，權刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Two years later he was released; Emperor Aizong comforted him at length, again made him libationer, passed through Vice Minister of Rites and Personnel, and acting Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was released. Emperor Aizong comforted him at length and again appointed him libationer. He later served as vice minister of both Rites and Personnel and as acting minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 明年，大元兵圍汴京，倉猝逃難，為騎兵所得，欲擁而北行。

translations.literal: The next year, Great Yuan troops besieged Bianjing; fleeing in haste he was seized by cavalry who wished to escort him north.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as Yuan forces besieged Bianjing, he fled in panic and was seized by cavalry who tried to hustle him north.

sentences.zh: 延登辭情慷慨，義不受辱，遂躍城旁井中，年五十八。

translations.literal: Yandeng spoke with lofty indignation, on principle would not accept humiliation, and leapt into a well beside the wall, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Yandeng answered with lofty indignation and, on principle, refused to endure humiliation. He leapt into a well beside the city wall. He was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 烏古孫仲端

translations.literal: Wugusun Zhongduan
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Zhongduan

sentences.zh: 烏古孫仲端，本名卜吉，字子正。

translations.literal: Wugusun Zhongduan, original name Buji, courtesy name Zizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Zhongduan, whose original name was Buji and whose courtesy name was Zizheng,

sentences.zh: 承安二年策論進士。

translations.literal: passed the jinshi in policy essays in the second year of Chengan.
translations.idiomatic: received his jinshi degree in policy essays in Chengan 2.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，累官禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanzong he rose through offices to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong he rose through the ranks to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 與翰林待制安延珍奉使乞和於大元，謁見太師國王木華黎，於是安延珍留止，仲端獨往。

translations.literal: With Hanlin awaiting editor An Yanzhen he went on embassy seeking peace with the Great Yuan and had audience with Grand Preceptor King Muqali; An Yanzhen was detained, and Zhongduan went on alone.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Hanlin awaiting editor An Yanzhen on an embassy to seek peace with the Yuan and had audience with Grand Preceptor King Muqali. An Yanzhen was detained, and Zhongduan continued alone.

sentences.zh: 並大夏，涉流沙，逾蔥嶺，至西域，進見太祖皇帝，致其使事乃還。

translations.literal: He passed through great Xia, crossed drifting sands, went over Congling, reached the Western Regions, had audience with Taizu, discharged his embassy duties, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through the great Xia state, crossed the drifting sands, crossed the Congling ranges, and reached the Western Regions, where he had audience with Taizu, completed his mission, and returned.

sentences.zh: 自興定四年七月啟行，明年十二月還至。

translations.literal: He set out in the seventh month of the fourth year of Xingding and returned in the twelfth month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: He departed in the seventh month of Xingding 4 and returned in the twelfth month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其有奉使勞，進官兩階，延珍進一階。

translations.literal: The court praised his embassy labors and advanced him two ranks; Yanzhen was advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his services on embassy and promoted him two ranks; Yanzhen was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 曆裕州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 正大元年，召為禦史中丞，奉詔安撫陝西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengda he was summoned as Censor-in-chief and by edict pacified Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 1 he was summoned to serve as censor-in-chief and by imperial edict was sent to pacify Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 及歸，權參知政事。

translations.literal: On his return he was acting Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as acting vice councilor.

sentences.zh: 正大五年十二月，知開封府事完顏麻斤出、吏部郎中楊居仁以奉使不職，尚書省具獄，有旨釋之備再使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Zhengda, Wanyan Majinchu, administrator of Kaifeng, and Yang Juren, director in the Ministry of Personnel, for failing in embassy duty had a full case prepared by the Ministry of Revenue; an order released them to serve again on embassy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhengda 5, Wanyan Majinchu, administrator of Kaifeng, and Yang Juren, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, were found to have failed in their embassy duties. The Ministry of Revenue prepared a full case against them, but an imperial order released them so they could be sent on embassy again.

sentences.zh: 仲端言曰；

translations.literal: Zhongduan said:
translations.idiomatic: Zhongduan said:

sentences.zh: 「麻斤出等辱君命，失臣節，大不敬，宜償禮幣誅之。」

translations.literal: " Majinchu and the others have shamed the sovereign's command, lost a minister's integrity, and committed great irreverence—they should compensate with ritual gifts and be executed."
translations.idiomatic: " Majinchu and the others have shamed the sovereign's command, betrayed a minister's duty, and committed grave irreverence. They should make restitution with ritual gifts and then be executed."

sentences.zh: 奏上，麻斤出等免死除名。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Majinchu and the others were spared death but dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Majinchu and the others were spared death but stripped of their offices.

sentences.zh: 會議降大軍事，及諍太后奉佛，涉亡家敗國之語，上怒，貶同州節度使。

translations.literal: When the council discussed surrendering to the main army and he remonstrated against the empress dowager's Buddhist devotion with words touching on ruin of house and state, the emperor was angry and demoted him to military commissioner of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the council discussed surrendering to the main army, he remonstrated against the empress dowager's Buddhist devotions in language that touched on the ruin of house and state. The emperor was enraged and demoted him to military commissioner of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 哀宗將遷歸德，召為翰林學士承旨，兼同簽大睦親府事，留守汴京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong was about to move to Guide, he was summoned as Hanlin academician recipient of edicts and concurrent associate commissioner of the Great Office of Imperial Kin, left to guard Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong prepared to move the court to Guide, Zhongduan was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician recipient of edicts and associate commissioner of the Great Office of Imperial Kin, and was left behind to guard Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 及大元兵圍汴，日久食盡，諸將不相統一，仲端自度汴中事變不測。

translations.literal: When Great Yuan troops besieged Bian, as days lengthened food was exhausted and the generals were not united; Zhongduan judged that events in Bian were unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan forces besieged Bian, supplies ran out as the siege dragged on and the generals could not act in concert. Zhongduan concluded that events in the city had become unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 一日與同年汝州防禦裴滿思忠小飲，談太學同舍事以為笑樂，因數言「人死亦易事耳。」

translations.literal: One day he drank lightly with his examination-year fellow Peiman Sizhong, defense commissioner of Ruzhou, talking of Imperial Academy dormitory matters for laughter, and repeatedly said: "For a man to die is also an easy thing."
translations.idiomatic: One day he shared a light drink with his examination-year fellow Peiman Sizhong, defense commissioner of Ruzhou. They reminisced about their Imperial Academy days with laughter, and Zhongduan said again and again, "For a man, dying is an easy thing."

sentences.zh: 思忠曰：「吾兄何故頻出此語？」

translations.literal: Sizhong said: "Elder brother, why do you keep saying this?"
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong asked, "Brother, why do you keep saying such things?"

sentences.zh: 仲端因寫一詩示之，其詩大概謂人生大似巢燕，或在華屋杏梁，或在村居茅茨，及秋社甫臨，皆當逝去。

translations.literal: Zhongduan then wrote a poem and showed it to him; the poem in general said human life greatly resembles nest-swallows, whether in splendid houses with apricot beams or in village dwellings of thatch—when autumn sacrifice just arrives, all must depart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongduan then wrote a poem and showed it to him. In essence it said that human life is much like swallows in a nest—whether in splendid mansions with carved beams or in thatched village cottages, when the autumn sacrifice arrives all must depart.

sentences.zh: 人生雖有富貴貧賤不同，要之終有一死耳。

translations.literal: Though human life differs in wealth and poverty, nobility and baseness, in the end there is only one death.
translations.idiomatic: Though men differ in wealth and rank, in the end there is only death.

sentences.zh: 書畢，連飲數杯，送思忠出門，曰：「此別終天矣。」

translations.literal: When he finished writing, he drank several cups in succession, saw Sizhong to the door, and said: "This parting is for all eternity."
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished writing, he drank several cups in succession and escorted Sizhong to the door, saying, "This parting is forever."

sentences.zh: 思忠去，仲端即自縊，其妻亦從死。

translations.literal: After Sizhong left, Zhongduan at once hanged himself, and his wife followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: After Sizhong left, Zhongduan hanged himself at once, and his wife died with him.

sentences.zh: 明日，崔立變。

translations.literal: The next day Cui Li mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cui Li staged his mutiny.

sentences.zh: 仲端為人樂易寬厚知大體，奉公好善，獨得士譽。

translations.literal: Zhongduan as a man was cheerful, easy, generous, and understood the larger pattern; he served the public and loved goodness, alone winning scholars' praise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongduan was cheerful, generous, and understood the larger pattern of affairs. He served the public zealously and loved what was good, and alone among officials won the praise of the scholarly class.

sentences.zh: 一子名愛實，嘗為護衛、奉禦，以誅官奴功授節度、世襲千戶。

translations.literal: One son named Aishi had served as guard and palace attendant; for the merit of executing the eunuch-official he was granted military commission and hereditary chiliarchy.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son, Aishi, who had served as an imperial guard and palace attendant. For killing the eunuch-official rebel he was granted a military commission and a hereditary chiliarchy.

sentences.zh: 思忠名正之，本名蒲剌篤，亦承安二年進士。

translations.literal: Sizhong's name was Zhengzhi, original name Puladu, also a jinshi of the second year of Chengan.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong, whose name was Zhengzhi and whose original name was Puladu, had also received his jinshi degree in Chengan 2.

sentences.zh: 烏古孫奴申

translations.literal: Wugusun Nushen
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Nushen

sentences.zh: 烏古孫奴申，字道遠。

translations.literal: Wugusun Nushen, courtesy name Daoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Nushen, whose courtesy name was Daoyuan,

sentences.zh: 由譯史入官。

translations.literal: entered office from translator-scribe.
translations.idiomatic: entered government service from the ranks of translator-scribes.

sentences.zh: 性伉特敢為，有直氣。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and daring, with a straight spirit.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and daring, with an unbending spirit.

sentences.zh: 嘗為監察禦史，時中丞完顏百家以酷烈聞，奴申以事糾罷，朝士聳然。

translations.literal: He once served as investigating censor; at the time Censor-in-chief Wanyan Baijia was known for cruelty; Nushen impeached and had him dismissed on grounds of an affair; court officials were startled.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as an investigating censor. At the time Censor-in-chief Wanyan Baijia was notorious for cruelty, and Nushen impeached him on specific grounds and had him dismissed—a deed that startled the court.

sentences.zh: 後為左司郎中、近侍局使，皆有名。

translations.literal: Later as director of the left department and commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau, in each he was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as director of the left department and as commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau, winning renown in each post.

sentences.zh: 哀宗東遷，為諫議大夫、近侍局使、行省左右司郎中、兼知宮省事，留汴京居守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved east, he was Remonstrance Grandee, Inner Service commissioner, Branch Secretariat director of left and right departments, and concurrent overseer of palace affairs, left at Bianjing to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong moved east, Nushen was made remonstrance grandee, commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau, director in the left and right departments of the Branch Secretariat, and concurrent overseer of palace affairs, and was left behind to hold Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 崔立變之明日，同御史大夫裴滿阿虎帶自縊死於台中。

translations.literal: The day after Cui Li's mutiny, together with Censor-in-chief Peiman Ahudai he hanged himself in the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Cui Li's mutiny, he and Censor-in-chief Peiman Ahudai hanged themselves in the censorate offices.

sentences.zh: 是日，戶部尚書完顏珠顆亦自縊。

translations.literal: That same day, Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke also hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke also hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 阿虎帶字仲寧，珠顆字仲平，皆女直進士。

translations.literal: Ahudai's courtesy name was Zhongning, Zhuke's was Zhongping; both were Jurchen jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ahudai's courtesy name was Zhongning and Zhuke's was Zhongping; both were Jurchen jinshi degree holders.

sentences.zh: 時不辱而死者，奉禦完顏忙哥、大睦親府事烏古孫仲端。

translations.literal: At the time those who died without accepting humiliation were palace attendant Wanyan Mangge and commissioner of the Great Office of Imperial Kin Wugusun Zhongduan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time those who died rather than accept humiliation included palace attendant Wanyan Mangge and commissioner of the Great Office of Imperial Kin Wugusun Zhongduan.

sentences.zh: 大理裴滿德輝、右副點檢完顏阿撒、參政完顏奴申之子麻因，可知者數人，餘各有傳。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian Peiman Dehui, right deputy inspector Wanyan Asa, Vice Councilor Wanyan Nushen's son Mayin—several such are known; the rest each have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian Peiman Dehui, right deputy inspector Wanyan Asa, and Vice Councilor Wanyan Nushen's son Mayin are among the few who can be named; the rest each have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 蒲察琦

translations.literal: Pucha Qi
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Qi

sentences.zh: 蒲察琦，本名阿憐，字仁卿，棣州陽信人。

translations.literal: Pucha Qi, original name Alian, courtesy name Renqing, a native of Yangxin in Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Qi, whose original name was Alian and whose courtesy name was Renqing, was a native of Yangxin in Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 試補刑部掾。

translations.literal: He passed examination and was appointed clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified by examination and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 兄世襲謀克，兄死，琦承襲。

translations.literal: His elder brother held a hereditary company commandership; when the brother died, Qi inherited it.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother held a hereditary company commandership, and when the brother died Qi inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 正大六年，秦、藍總帥府辟琦為安平都尉粘葛合典下都統兼知事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengda, the Qin-Lan commander-in-chief's headquarters recruited Qi as overall commander under Anping Commander Niange Hedan, with concurrent administrative duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 6 the Qin-Lan command headquarters recruited Qi to serve as overall commander under Anping Commander Niange Hedan, with concurrent administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 其冬，小關破，事勢已迫。

translations.literal: That winter Xiaoguan fell and the situation was already pressing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xiaoguan fell, and the military situation had already become desperate.

sentences.zh: 琦常在合典左右，合典令避矢石，琦不去，曰：「業已從公，死生當共之，尚安所避耶。」

translations.literal: Qi was constantly at Hedan's side; Hedan ordered him to avoid arrows and stones; Qi would not leave, saying: "Having already followed you, life and death should be shared—where else is there to flee?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi stayed constantly at Hedan's side. When Hedan ordered him to keep clear of arrows and stones, Qi refused to leave, saying, "I have already cast my lot with you—life and death should be shared. Where else would I go?"

sentences.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，汴京立講議所，受陳言文字，其官則御史大夫納合甯以下十七人，皆朝臣之選，而琦以有論議預焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Bianjing established a Discussion Office to receive submitted proposals; its officers were seventeen from Censor-in-chief Nahaning down, all chosen courtiers, and Qi for his policy discussion was included.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Bianjing established a Discussion Office to receive public proposals. Its officers numbered seventeen from Censor-in-chief Nahaning downward, all selected courtiers, and Qi was included because of his reputation for policy debate.

sentences.zh: 時左司都事元好問領講議，兼看讀陳言文字，與琦甚相得。

translations.literal: At the time Left Department chief clerk Yuan Haowen headed the discussions and concurrently reviewed submitted proposals; he and Qi were very close.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Haowen, chief clerk of the Left Department, headed the discussions and also reviewed submitted proposals; he and Qi became very close.

sentences.zh: 崔立變後，令改易巾髻，琦謂好問曰：「今日易巾髻，在京人皆可，獨琦不可。

translations.literal: After Cui Li's mutiny, an order came to change caps and topknots; Qi told Haowen: "Today to change caps and topknots—all in the capital may, but Qi alone may not.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Li's mutiny, an order came to change caps and topknots. Qi told Haowen, "Everyone in the capital may do this today—but I cannot.

sentences.zh: 琦一刑部譯史，襲先兄世爵，安忍作此？

translations.literal: Qi is but a translator-scribe of Punishments who inherited his elder brother's hereditary title—how could I bear to do this?
translations.idiomatic: I am only a translator-scribe in the Ministry of Punishments who inherited my elder brother's hereditary title—how could I endure doing this?

sentences.zh: 今以一死付公。

translations.literal: Now I entrust my death to you.
translations.idiomatic: I now entrust my death to you.

sentences.zh: 然死則即死，付公一言亦剩矣。」

translations.literal: Yet if I die, I die at once—even entrusting one word to you is surplus."
translations.idiomatic: But if I am to die, let me die at once—even asking you to remember one word is more than I need."

sentences.zh: 因泣涕而別。

translations.literal: He then parted in tears.
translations.idiomatic: He parted from him in tears.

sentences.zh: 琦既至其家，母氏方晝寢，驚而寤。

translations.literal: When Qi reached his home, his mother was napping at midday and woke with a start.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi reached home, his mother had been napping at midday and woke with a start.

sentences.zh: 琦問阿母何為，母曰：「適夢三人潛伏梁間，故驚寤。」

translations.literal: Qi asked his mother what was the matter; she said: "I just dreamed three men lurking among the beams, hence I woke startled."
translations.idiomatic: Qi asked what had happened. His mother said, "I dreamed just now that three men were lurking in the rafters—that is why I woke in alarm."

sentences.zh: 仁卿跪曰：「梁上人，鬼也。

translations.literal: Renqing knelt and said: "Men on the beams are ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Renqing knelt and said, "Men in the rafters are ghosts.

sentences.zh: 兒意在懸樑，阿母夢先見耳。」

translations.literal: Your son intends to hang from a beam—mother's dream saw it first, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Your son means to hang himself from a beam—your dream saw it first, that is all."

sentences.zh: 家人輩泣勸曰：「君不念老母歟？」

translations.literal: The household wept and urged: "Sir, do you not think of your aged mother?"
translations.idiomatic: His family wept and pleaded, "Do you not think of your aged mother?"

sentences.zh: 母止之曰：「勿勸，兒所處是矣。」

translations.literal: His mother stopped them: "Do not urge him—my son's place is decided."
translations.idiomatic: His mother stopped them. "Do not plead with him—my son has made his decision."

sentences.zh: 即自縊，時年四十餘。

translations.literal: He at once hanged himself, aged over forty.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself at once. He was in his forties.

sentences.zh: 琦性沉靜好讀書，知古今事。

translations.literal: Qi's nature was calm and he loved reading, knowing affairs ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was calm by nature, loved reading, and was well versed in affairs ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 其母完顏氏，以孝謹稱。

translations.literal: His mother of the Wanyan clan was known for filial piety and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Wanyan clan, was renowned for filial piety and prudent conduct.

sentences.zh: 蔡八兒

translations.literal: Cai Baer
translations.idiomatic: Cai Baer

sentences.zh: 蔡八兒，不知其所始。

translations.literal: Cai Baer—his origins are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Baer—nothing is known of his origins.

sentences.zh: 矯捷有勇，性純質可任。

translations.literal: Agile and brave, by nature simple and trustworthy, fit for responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He was agile and brave, and by nature so straightforward and trustworthy that he could be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 時為忠孝軍元帥。

translations.literal: At the time he was commander of the Loyalty and Filiality Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he commanded the Loyalty and Filiality Army.

sentences.zh: 天興二年，自息州入援，會大將奔盞遣數百騎駐城東，令人大呼曰：「城中速降，當免殺戮，不然無噍類矣。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxing, coming from Xi Prefecture to reinforce, it happened that Grand General Benzhai sent several hundred horsemen to encamp east of the city and had men shout loudly: "Surrender quickly in the city and slaughter will be spared; otherwise none will be left alive."
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing 2 he came from Xi Prefecture to reinforce the city. Grand General Benzhai sent several hundred horsemen to encamp east of the walls and had men shout, "Surrender at once and you will be spared slaughter; otherwise not one of you will survive."

sentences.zh: 於是，上登城，遣八兒率挽強兵百餘潛出暗門，渡汝水，左右交射之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor mounted the wall and sent Baer leading over a hundred strong-draw archers to slip out through a hidden gate, cross the Ru River, and shoot at them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then mounted the wall and sent Baer with more than a hundred powerful archers to slip out through a hidden gate, cross the Ru River, and shoot at the enemy from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 自是兵不復薄城，築長壘為久困計。

translations.literal: From then on the troops no longer pressed the city and built long ramparts for a plan of prolonged siege.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the enemy no longer pressed close to the walls and instead built long ramparts for a prolonged siege.

sentences.zh: 上令分軍防守四城，以殿前都點檢兀林答胡土守西面，八兒副之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered troops divided to defend the four walls; Palace Chief Inspector Ulin Hu'utu held the west face with Baer as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor divided his forces to defend the four walls of the city, placing Palace Chief Inspector Ulin Hu'utu on the west face with Baer as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 已而哀宗度蔡城不守，傳位承麟。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Aizong judged that Cai could not be held and passed the throne to Chenglang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Aizong concluded that Cai could not be held and abdicated in favor of Chenglang.

sentences.zh: 群臣入賀，班定，八兒不拜，謂所親曰：「事至於此，有死而已，安能更事一君乎！」

translations.literal: The ministers entered to congratulate; when the ranks were set, Baer did not bow and told those close to him: "Matters have come to this—there is only death; how could I serve another lord!"
translations.idiomatic: The ministers entered to offer congratulations. When the ranks were formed, Baer refused to bow and told those close to him, "Matters have come to this—there is only death. How could I serve another sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 遂戰死。

translations.literal: He then died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He then died fighting.

sentences.zh: 毛牷者，恩州人。

translations.literal: Mao Quan was a man of En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Quan was a native of En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞祐中為盜，宣宗南渡，率眾歸國，署為義軍招撫。

translations.literal: In Zhenyou he was a bandit; when Emperor Xuanzong crossed south he led his followers to submit to the state and was appointed pacification commissioner of the Loyalty Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyou era he had been a bandit leader. When Emperor Xuanzong crossed the river south, he led his followers to submit and was appointed pacification commissioner of the Loyalty Army.

sentences.zh: 哀宗遷蔡，以牷為都尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Cai, he made Quan commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong moved the court to Cai, he appointed Quan a commander.

sentences.zh: 圍城之戰。

translations.literal: In the siege battles
translations.idiomatic: In the siege battles

sentences.zh: 牷力居多，城破自縊。

translations.literal: Quan's effort was greatest; when the city fell he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Quan contributed the greatest effort. When the city fell he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 其子先牷戰歿。

translations.literal: His son had died in battle before Quan.
translations.idiomatic: His son had already died in battle before him.

sentences.zh: 時死事者則有閻忠、郝乙、王阿驢、樊喬焉。

translations.literal: At the time those who died in the cause included Yan Zhong, Hao Yi, Wang Alu, and Fan Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time others who died in the city's defense included Yan Zhong, Hao Yi, Wang Alu, and Fan Qiao.

sentences.zh: 忠，滑州人。

translations.literal: Zhong was a man of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was a native of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 衛王時，開州剌史賽哥叛，忠單騎入城，縛賽哥以出，由是漸被擢用。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Wei, Kaizhou prefect Saige rebelled; Zhong entered the city alone on horseback, bound Saige and brought him out, and thereby was gradually promoted.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Wei, Saige, prefect of Kaizhou, rebelled. Zhong rode alone into the city, bound Saige, and brought him out. Thereafter he was gradually promoted.

sentences.zh: 乙，磁州人，同日戰死，哀宗贈官。

translations.literal: Yi was a man of Ci Prefecture; he died in battle the same day and Emperor Aizong posthumously awarded him office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a native of Ci Prefecture. He died in battle on the same day, and Emperor Aizong posthumously enfeoffed him.

sentences.zh: 阿驢、樊喬，皆河中人，初為砲軍萬戶。

translations.literal: Alu and Fan Qiao were both men of Hezhong, initially commanders of ten thousands in the artillery army.
translations.idiomatic: Alu and Fan Qiao were both natives of Hezhong and had originally served as commanders of ten thousands in the artillery army.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔破，北降，從軍攻汴，司砲如故，即紿主者曰：「砲利於短，不利於長。」

translations.literal: When Fengxiang fell they surrendered northward, followed the army to attack Bian, still directing artillery, and deceived their superiors saying: "Artillery is advantageous short, not advantageous long."
translations.idiomatic: When Fengxiang fell they surrendered to the north and followed the army in the attack on Bian, still directing the artillery. They deceived their superiors, saying, "Catapults are effective when short, not when long."

sentences.zh: 信之，使截其木數尺、綆十餘握，由是機雖起伏，所擊無力。

translations.literal: They believed it and had the timbers cut by several feet and the ropes by more than ten handspans; thus though the machines rose and fell, the strikes had no force.
translations.idiomatic: Their superiors believed them and had the timbers shortened by several feet and the ropes cut by more than ten handspans. Though the machines still moved up and down, their blows had no force.

sentences.zh: 即日二人皆捐家走城。

translations.literal: That same day both men abandoned their households and fled to the city.
translations.idiomatic: That same day both men abandoned their households and fled into the city.

sentences.zh: 是時，女直人無死事者，長公主言于哀宗曰：「近來立功效命多諸色人，無事時則自家人爭強，有事則他人盡力，焉得不怨。」

translations.literal: At the time no Jurchen died in the cause; the Senior Princess said to Emperor Aizong: "Recently those who establish merit and give their lives are mostly men of various colors; in quiet times our own people vie for power, in crisis others exert themselves—how could there be no resentment."
translations.idiomatic: At the time no Jurchen had died in the city's defense. The Senior Princess said to Emperor Aizong, "Recently those who have won merit and given their lives have mostly been men of other ethnic groups. In peaceful times our own people vie for power; in crisis others do the fighting. How could there be no resentment?"

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 餘各有傳。

translations.literal: The rest each have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The rest each have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 溫敦昌孫

translations.literal: Wendun Changsun
translations.idiomatic: Wendun Changsun

sentences.zh: 溫敦昌孫，皇太后之侄，衛尉七十五之子。

translations.literal: Wendun Changsun, nephew of the empress dowager, son of Grand Guard Qishiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wendun Changsun was a nephew of the empress dowager and the son of Grand Guard Qishiwu.

sentences.zh: 為人短小精悍，性複愷弟。

translations.literal: As a man he was short, keen, and spirited, and by nature again kind and easy.
translations.idiomatic: He was short in stature but keen and spirited, and by nature kindly and easygoing.

sentences.zh: 累遷諸局分官。

translations.literal: He rose through offices in the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through a series of posts in the various palace bureaus.

sentences.zh: 上幸蔡，授殿前左副點檢。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Cai, he was appointed left deputy inspector before the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to Cai, he was appointed left deputy inspector before the palace.

sentences.zh: 圍城中，數引軍潛出巡邏。

translations.literal: During the siege, several times he led troops out in secret to patrol the perimeter.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege he repeatedly led troops out in secret to patrol the perimeter.

sentences.zh: 時尚食須魚，汝河魚甚美，上以水多浮屍，惡之。

translations.literal: At the time the Imperial Kitchen required fish; the Ru River fish were very fine, but the emperor loathed them because the water held many floating corpses.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Kitchen then needed fish. The Ru River fish were excellent, but the emperor refused them because so many corpses floated in the water.

sentences.zh: 城西有積水曰練江，魚大且多，往捕必軍衛乃可。

translations.literal: West of the city there was accumulated water called Lian River; the fish were large and numerous, yet going to catch them required a military escort to be possible.
translations.idiomatic: West of the city lay a body of water called Lian River, where the fish were large and plentiful—but fishing there required an armed escort.

sentences.zh: 昌孫常自領兵以往，所得動千餘斤，分賜將士。

translations.literal: Changsun often personally led troops to go; what he obtained routinely exceeded a thousand jin, which he divided and bestowed on officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun often led the troops himself. Each haul routinely exceeded a thousand jin, which he distributed among the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 後知其出，左右設伏，伺而邀之，力戰而死。

translations.literal: Later [the enemy] learned of his outings; they set ambushes on both flanks, waited and intercepted him, and he died fighting with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy eventually learned of these outings, set ambushes on both flanks, and lay in wait to intercept him. He fought fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 蔡城破，前監察禦史納坦胡失打聞之，慟哭，投水而死。

translations.literal: When Cai city fell, the former censor Nataan Hushida heard of it, wailed bitterly, and drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai fell, the former censor Nataan Hushida heard the news, wept bitterly, and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 完顏絳山

translations.literal: Wanyan Jiangshan
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Jiangshan

sentences.zh: 完顏絳山，哀宗之奉禦也，系出始祖。

translations.literal: Wanyan Jiangshan was Emperor Aizong's palace attendant, descended from the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Jiangshan was a palace attendant to Emperor Aizong and traced his lineage to the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 天興二年十月，蔡城被圍，城中饑民萬余訴於有司求出，有司難之，民大呼於道。
