translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Tianxing, Cai city was besieged; more than ten thousand starving people in the city petitioned the authorities to be let out, the authorities found it difficult, and the people shouted loudly in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Tianxing, as Cai was under siege, more than ten thousand starving townspeople petitioned the authorities to leave the city. The officials hesitated, and the people cried out in the streets.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，遣近侍官分監四門，門日出千人，必老稚羸疾者聽其出。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and sent palace attendants to supervise the four gates separately; each gate was to release a thousand people per day, and only the old, young, weak, and sick were to be allowed out.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he sent palace attendants to supervise the four gates. Each gate was to release a thousand people daily, but only the elderly, children, the weak, and the sick were permitted to leave.

sentences.zh: 絳山時在北門，憫人之饑，出過其數，命杖之四十。

translations.literal: Jiangshan was then at the north gate; pitying the people's hunger, he let out more than the allotted number and was ordered beaten forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangshan was then stationed at the north gate. Moved by the people's hunger, he allowed more than the quota to leave and was ordered flogged forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 然出者多泄城中虛實，尋止之。

translations.literal: Yet those who went out often leaked the city's true condition, and soon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: But those who left often revealed the city's true condition, and the policy was soon halted.

sentences.zh: 三年正月己酉，蔡城破，哀宗傳立承麟，即自縊于幽蘭軒。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the first month of the third year, Cai city fell; Emperor Aizong had Chenglang proclaimed [successor] and immediately hanged himself in Youlan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the first month of the third year, Cai fell. Emperor Aizong had Chenglang proclaimed as his successor and then hanged himself in Youlan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 權點檢內族斜烈矯制召承禦石盞氏、近侍局大使焦春和、內侍局殿頭宋珪赴上前，曉以名分大義，及侍從官巴良弼、阿勒根文卿皆從死。

translations.literal: Acting Inspector of the Inner Clan Xielie forged an edict summoning Attendant Lady Shizhan of the Shi clan, Grand Master of the Attendants Bureau Jiao Chunhe, and Head Clerk of the Inner Attendants Bureau Song Gui before the emperor, explaining the great principle of rightful status; attendants Balangbi and Aligen Wenqing all followed him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Inspector of the Inner Clan Xielie forged an edict summoning Attendant Lady Shizhan, Grand Master of the Attendants Bureau Jiao Chunhe, and Head Clerk of the Inner Attendants Bureau Song Gui to the emperor's presence, where he explained the duty owed to one's sovereign. Attendants Balangbi and Aligen Wenqing all followed him to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 斜烈將死，遺言絳山，使焚幽蘭軒。

translations.literal: As Xielie was about to die, he left word to Jiangshan, ordering him to burn Youlan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: As Xielie was about to die, he left instructions with Jiangshan to burn Youlan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 火方熾，子城破，大兵突入，近侍左右皆走避，獨絳山留不去，為兵所執，問曰：「汝為誰？」

translations.literal: The fire was just blazing when the inner city fell; the great army burst in, and the attendants on left and right all fled and hid—only Jiangshan remained and would not leave. He was seized by soldiers, who asked, "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: The fire was still blazing when the inner city fell and the Mongol forces burst in. The attendants all fled—only Jiangshan stayed behind. Soldiers seized him and asked, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 絳山曰：「吾奉禦絳山也。」

translations.literal: Jiangshan said, "I am the palace attendant Jiangshan."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangshan replied, "I am the palace attendant Jiangshan."

sentences.zh: 兵曰：「眾皆散走，而獨後何也？」

translations.literal: The soldier said, "All have scattered and fled—why do you alone stay behind?"
translations.idiomatic: The soldier said, "Everyone else has fled—why do you alone remain?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾君終於是，吾候火滅灰寒，收瘞其骨耳。」

translations.literal: He said, "My lord ended here; I wait until the fire dies and the ashes grow cold to gather and bury his bones, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "My lord died here. I mean only to wait until the fire dies and the ashes grow cold, then gather and bury his bones."

sentences.zh: 兵笑曰：「若狂者耶？

translations.literal: The soldier laughed and said, "Like a madman, are you?
translations.idiomatic: The soldier laughed. "Are you mad?

sentences.zh: 汝命且不能保，能瘞而君耶？」

translations.literal: Your life cannot even be preserved—can you bury your lord?"
translations.idiomatic: You cannot even save your own life—how can you bury your lord?"

sentences.zh: 絳山曰：「人各事其君。

translations.literal: Jiangshan said, "Each person serves his own lord.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangshan said, "Every man serves his own lord.

sentences.zh: 吾君有天下十餘年，功業弗終，身死社稷，忍使暴露遺骸與士卒等耶？

translations.literal: My lord held the realm for more than ten years; his achievement was not completed, and he died for the altars of state—how could I bear to leave his exposed remains equal to common soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: My lord held the realm for more than ten years, yet his work was left unfinished when he died for the state. How could I bear to let his exposed remains lie no better than those of common soldiers?

sentences.zh: 吾逆知君輩必不遺吾，吾是以留。

translations.literal: I foreknew that you would surely not spare me—that is why I stayed.
translations.idiomatic: I knew beforehand that you would not spare me—that is why I stayed.

sentences.zh: 果瘞吾君之後，雖寸斬吾不恨矣。」

translations.literal: If after truly burying my lord, even execution by inch-long cuts, I would bear no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Once I have buried my lord, even if I am cut to pieces I will have no regret."

sentences.zh: 兵以告其帥，奔盞曰：「此奇男子也。」

translations.literal: The soldiers reported it to their commander; Benzhai said, "This is an extraordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers reported this to their commander. Benzhai said, "This is an extraordinary man."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: He granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: He granted his request.

sentences.zh: 絳山乃掇其餘燼，裹以弊衾，瘞于汝水之旁。

translations.literal: Jiangshan then gathered the remaining embers, wrapped them in a worn quilt, and buried them beside the Ru River.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangshan gathered the remaining embers, wrapped them in a worn quilt, and buried them beside the Ru River.

sentences.zh: 再拜號哭，將赴汝水死。

translations.literal: He bowed twice, wailed aloud, and was about to go to the Ru River to die.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice, wailed aloud, and was about to throw himself into the Ru River.

sentences.zh: 軍士救之得免，後不知所終。

translations.literal: Soldiers rescued him and he escaped death; afterward his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers rescued him in time. What became of him afterward is unknown.

sentences.zh: 畢資倫，縉山人也。

translations.literal: Bi Zilun was a native of Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zilun was a native of Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 泰和南征，以傭雇從軍，軍還，例授進義副尉。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign in Taihe he followed the army as a hired soldier; when the army returned he was by precedent appointed vice-warden of Jinyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign in Taihe he followed the army as a hired soldier; when the army returned he was by precedent appointed vice-warden of Jinyi.

sentences.zh: 崇慶元年，改縉山為鎮州，朮虎高琪為防禦使、行元帥府事於是州，選資倫為防城軍千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongqing Jinshan was changed to Zhen Prefecture. Paihu Gaoqi served as defense commissioner and acting commander-in-chief's headquarters at that prefecture and selected Zilun as commander of a thousand of the defense army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongqing Jinshan was changed to Zhen Prefecture. Paihu Gaoqi served as defense commissioner and acting commander-in-chief's headquarters there and selected Zilun as commander of a thousand of the defense army.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年秋，大元兵至鎮州，高琪棄城遁。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Zhi'ning the Great Yuan army reached Zhen Prefecture and Gaoqi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Zhi'ning the Great Yuan army reached Zhen Prefecture and Gaoqi abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 資倫行及昌平，收避遷民兵，轉戰有功，擢授都統軍。

translations.literal: Zilun had reached Changping. He gathered militia who had fled the relocation and fought with merit, and was promoted to overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun had reached Changping. He gathered militia who had fled the relocation, fought with merit, and was promoted to overall commander.

sentences.zh: 軍數千，與軍中將領沉思忠、寧子都輩同隸一府，屯鄭州及衛州，時號「沈、畢軍」。

translations.literal: His army numbered several thousand. Together with the commanders Shen Sizhong, Ning Zidu, and others he served under one headquarters, garrisoned at Zheng and Wei prefectures, and at the time was called the "Shen-Bi Army."
translations.idiomatic: His army numbered several thousand. Together with the commanders Shen Sizhong, Ning Zidu, and others he served under one headquarters, garrisoned at Zheng and Wei prefectures, and at the time was called the "Shen-Bi Army."

sentences.zh: 積功至都總領，思忠為副都尉。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he rose to overall commander; Sizhong served as deputy commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he rose to overall commander; Sizhong served as deputy commandant.

sentences.zh: 僕散阿海南征，軍次梅林關不得過，阿海問諸將誰能取此關者，資倫首出應命。

translations.literal: Pusan Ahai marched south; his army halted at Meilin Pass and could not pass. Ahai asked the generals who could take this pass, and Zilun was the first to step forward and accept the mission.
translations.idiomatic: On Pusan Ahai's southern campaign, his army halted at Meilin Pass and could not get through. Ahai asked his generals who could take the pass, and Zilun was the first to volunteer.

sentences.zh: 問須軍士幾何，曰：「止用資倫所統足矣，不煩餘軍。」

translations.literal: Asked how many soldiers were needed, he said, "Only those under Zilun's command will suffice; there is no need to trouble other troops."
translations.idiomatic: When asked how many men he needed, he said, "My own command is enough. There is no need to call on other units."

sentences.zh: 明日遲明，出宋軍不意，引兵簿之，萬眾崩，遂取梅林關。

translations.literal: The next day near dawn, catching the Song army unawares, he led troops to press close upon it; the ten thousand troops collapsed, and thus Meilin Pass was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning at dawn he caught the Song army by surprise, pressed his troops against them, and routed their force of ten thousand. Meilin Pass was taken.

sentences.zh: 阿海軍得南行，留提控王祿軍萬人守關。

translations.literal: Ahai's army was able to march south; he left Commander Wang Lu with ten thousand troops to guard the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ahai's army was able to continue south. He left Commander Wang Lu with ten thousand men to hold the pass.

sentences.zh: 不數日，宋兵奪關守之，阿海以梅林歸途為敵據，計無所出，複問：「誰能取梅林者，以帥職賞之。」

translations.literal: Within a few days the Song army retook the pass and held it; Ahai's route of return through Meilin was held by the enemy, and he had no plan. He again asked, "Who can retake Meilin? I will reward him with a commander's post."
translations.idiomatic: Within days the Song retook the pass. With the Meilin route home now in enemy hands, Ahai had no solution. He asked again, "Who can retake Meilin? I will reward him with a commander's rank."

sentences.zh: 資倫複出應命，以本軍再奪梅林。

translations.literal: Zilun again stepped forward to accept the mission and, with his own army, retook Meilin once more.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun volunteered again and, leading his own troops, retook Meilin.

sentences.zh: 阿海破蘄、黃，按軍而還，論功資論第一，授遙領同知昌武軍節度使、宣差總領都提控。

translations.literal: Ahai took Qi and Huang, pressed the army and returned; in assessing merit Zilun ranked first. He was appointed honorary acting co-administrator of the Changwu Army command, commissioner general and chief overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Ahai captured Qi and Huang and marched home, Zilun was ranked first in merit. He received an honorary appointment as acting co-administrator of the Changwu Army command and was made commissioner general and chief overall commander.

sentences.zh: 既而樞密院以資倫、思忠不相能，恐敗事，以資倫統本軍屯泗州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Privy Council, because Zilun and Sizhong could not get along and feared failure of the mission, posted Zilun to garrison Sizhou at the head of his own army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Privy Council, fearing that Zilun and Sizhong could not work together and would ruin the mission, posted Zilun with his own army to garrison Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 興定五年正月戊戌，提控王祿湯餅會軍中宴飲，宋龜山統制時青乘隙襲破泗州西城。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the first month of the fifth year of Xingding, Commander Wang Lu held a noodle feast and banquet drinking in the camp; Song Guishan commander Shi Qing seized the opening, raided, and broke through Sizhou's west city.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the first month of the fifth year of Xingding, Commander Wang Lu held a noodle feast and drinking party in camp. Song commander Shi Qing of Guishan seized the opportunity, raided, and broke through the west wall of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 資倫知失計，墮南城求死，為宋軍所執，以見時青。

translations.literal: Zilun knew the plan had failed; he leaped from the south wall seeking death, was seized by the Song army, and was brought before Shi Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing all was lost, Zilun leaped from the south wall in an attempt to die. Song troops seized him and brought him before Shi Qing.

sentences.zh: 青說之曰：「畢宣差，我知爾好男子，亦宜相時達變。

translations.literal: Qing persuaded him, saying, "Commissioner Bi, I know you are a fine man; you should also read the times and adapt to change.
translations.idiomatic: Qing tried to persuade him: "Commissioner Bi, I know you are a man of worth. You ought to read the times and adapt.

sentences.zh: 金國勢已衰弱，爾肯降我，宋亦不負爾。

translations.literal: The Jin state's power is already weakened; if you are willing to surrender to me, Song too will not fail you.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin state is already in decline. If you surrender to me, Song will not treat you badly.

sentences.zh: 若不從，見劉天帥即死矣。」

translations.literal: If you do not comply, the moment you see Marshal Liu you will die."
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, you will die the moment you are brought before Marshal Liu."

sentences.zh: 資倫極口罵曰：「時青逆賊聽我言。

translations.literal: Zilun cursed with all his might, saying, "Shi Qing, rebel traitor—hear my words.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun cursed him roundly: "Shi Qing, you rebel traitor—hear me.

sentences.zh: 我出身至貧賤，結柳器為生，自征南始得一官，今職居三品。

translations.literal: My origin was utterly poor and low; I made a living weaving willow vessels. Only from the southern campaign did I first receive an office; now my rank stands at the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: I came from the humblest poverty and made my living weaving willow baskets. I did not receive an office until the southern campaign, and now I hold third rank.

sentences.zh: 不幸失國家城池，甘分一死尚不能報，肯從汝反賊求生耶！」

translations.literal: Unfortunate though I lost the state's city, even willingly accepting death I still cannot repay my debt—would I follow you, rebel traitor, to seek life?"
translations.idiomatic: I have already lost a city of the state. Even death willingly accepted would not repay my debt—would I follow a rebel traitor like you to save my life?"

sentences.zh: 青知無降意，下盱眙獄。

translations.literal: Qing knew he had no intention of surrendering and sent him down to the Xuyi prison.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Zilun would not surrender, Qing had him thrown into the prison at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 時臨淮令李某者亦被執，後得歸，為泗州從宜移剌羊哥言其事。

translations.literal: At the time a certain Magistrate Li of Linhuai was also captured; later he returned and reported the matter to Sizhou adjutant Yila Yangge.
translations.idiomatic: A Magistrate Li of Linhuai had also been captured at the time. After he returned, he recounted the affair to Sizhou adjutant Yila Yangge.

sentences.zh: 羊哥以資倫惡語罵時青必被殺，即以死不屈節聞於朝。

translations.literal: Yangge, because Zilun had cursed Shi Qing with harsh words and would surely be killed, reported to the court that he had died without yielding his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yangge assumed that Zilun's fierce curses at Shi Qing meant he would be killed, and reported to the court that he had died without surrendering his integrity.

sentences.zh: 時資倫子牛兒年十二，居宿州，收充皇后位奉閣舍人。

translations.literal: At the time Zilun's son Niuer was twelve years old, living in Suzhou; he was taken in and appointed an attendant of the empress's pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zilun's son Niuer was twelve and living in Suzhou. He was taken into service as an attendant in the empress's pavilion.

sentences.zh: 宋人亦賞資倫忠憤不撓，欲全活之，鈐以鐵繩，囚於鎮江府土獄，略給衣食使不至寒餓，脅誘百方，時一引出問雲：「汝降否？」

translations.literal: The Song also admired Zilun's loyal indignation and unyielding spirit and wished to keep him alive; they shackled him with iron chains and imprisoned him in the earthen prison of Zhenjiang Prefecture, giving him just enough food and clothing so he would not suffer cold or hunger. They tried every means of coercion and persuasion, and from time to time brought him out and asked, "Will you surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: The Song also admired Zilun's loyal fury and unbending spirit and wanted to keep him alive. They bound him with iron chains and held him in the earthen prison at Zhenjiang Prefecture, giving him barely enough food and clothing to keep him from freezing or starving. They tried every form of coercion and persuasion, and from time to time brought him out to ask, "Will you surrender?"

sentences.zh: 資倫或罵或不語，如是十四年。

translations.literal: Zilun either cursed or said nothing; thus it went for fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun either cursed them or kept silent. This continued for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 及盱眙將士降宋，宋使總帥納合買住已下北望哭拜，謂之辭故主，驅資倫在旁觀之。

translations.literal: When the officers and soldiers of Xuyi surrendered to Song, the Song had Grand Marshal Nahe Maizhu and those below him face north, weep, and bow, calling it taking leave of their former lord; they drove Zilun to watch at their side.
translations.idiomatic: When the officers and men of Xuyi surrendered to Song, the Song made Grand Marshal Nahe Maizhu and his subordinates face north, weep, and bow in farewell to their former sovereign. They forced Zilun to watch from the side.

sentences.zh: 資倫見買住罵曰：「納合買住，國家未嘗負汝，何所求死不可，乃作如此觜鼻耶！」

translations.literal: Zilun saw Maizhu and cursed, saying, "Nahe Maizhu, the state never failed you—what is there that death cannot satisfy, that you make such a shameful display!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zilun saw Maizhu he cursed him: "Nahe Maizhu, the state never wronged you. What is there that death cannot answer—why put on such a shameful show!"

sentences.zh: 買住俯首不敢仰視。

translations.literal: Maizhu bowed his head and did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: Maizhu bowed his head and did not dare meet his eyes.

sentences.zh: 及蔡州破，哀宗自縊，宋人以告資倫。

translations.literal: When Caizhou fell and Emperor Aizong hanged himself, the Song told Zilun.
translations.idiomatic: When Caizhou fell and Emperor Aizong hanged himself, the Song informed Zilun.

sentences.zh: 資倫歎曰：「吾無所望矣。

translations.literal: Zilun sighed and said, "I have nothing left to hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun sighed. "I have nothing left to hope for.

sentences.zh: 容我一祭吾君乃降耳。」

translations.literal: Allow me one offering to my lord, and then I will surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to make one offering to my lord, and then I will surrender."

sentences.zh: 宋人信之，為屠牛羊設祭鎮江南岸。

translations.literal: The Song believed him, slaughtered cattle and sheep, and set up the offering on the south bank of the Yangzi at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Song believed him. They slaughtered cattle and sheep and set up the offering on the south bank of the Yangzi at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 資倫祭畢，伏地大哭，乘其不防投江水而死。

translations.literal: When Zilun had finished the offering, he prostrated himself and wailed loudly; seizing their inattention he threw himself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, Zilun prostrated himself and wailed. Then, catching them off guard, he threw himself into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 宋人義之，宣示四方，仍議為立祠。

translations.literal: The Song honored his righteousness, proclaimed it in all directions, and further discussed erecting a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Song honored his conduct, proclaimed it throughout the realm, and even discussed building a shrine in his memory.

sentences.zh: 鎮江之囚有方士者親嘗見之，以告元好問，及言泗州城陷資倫被執事，且曰：「資倫長身，面赤色，顴頰微高，髯疏而黃。

translations.literal: Among the prisoners at Zhenjiang there was a Daoist who had personally seen him; he told Yuan Haowen, and also spoke of the fall of Sizhou and Zilun's capture, saying, "Zilun was tall of body, with a ruddy face, slightly high cheekbones, and a sparse yellow beard.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist among the prisoners at Zhenjiang had seen him in person and told Yuan Haowen about the fall of Sizhou and Zilun's capture. He said, "Zilun was tall, with a ruddy face, slightly high cheekbones, and a sparse yellow beard.

sentences.zh: 資稟質直，重然諾，故其堅忍守節卓卓如此。」

translations.literal: By nature he was upright of character and valued his word; therefore his steadfast endurance in keeping his integrity stood out so remarkably."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and kept his word faithfully; that is why he endured and held to his integrity so remarkably."

sentences.zh: 《宣宗實錄》載資倫為亂兵所殺，當時傳聞不得其實雲。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong record that Zilun was killed by mutinous troops; the rumors of the time did not get at the truth, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong say that Zilun was killed by mutinous troops—the rumors of the day did not capture what really happened.

sentences.zh: 郭蝦蟆

translations.literal: Guo Xiama
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiama

sentences.zh: 郭蝦蟆，會州人。

translations.literal: Guo Xiama was a man of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiama was a native of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 世為保甲射生手，與兄祿大俱以善射應募。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been baojia archery hunters; he and his elder brother Ludu both enlisted for their skill in shooting.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served for generations as baojia archery hunters. He and his elder brother Ludu both enlisted for their skill as marksmen.

sentences.zh: 興定初，祿大以功遷遙授同知平涼府事、兼會州刺史，進官一階，賜姓顏盞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingding, Ludu was transferred for merit to honorary acting co-administrator of Pingliang Prefecture and concurrent prefect of Huizhou, advanced one rank in office, and granted the surname Yanzhan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xingding era, Ludu was promoted for merit to honorary acting co-administrator of Pingliang Prefecture and concurrent prefect of Huizhou. He was advanced one rank and granted the surname Yanzhan.

sentences.zh: 夏人攻會州，祿大遙見其主兵者人馬皆衣金，出入陣中，約二百余步，一發中其吭，殪之。

translations.literal: When the Tangut attacked Huizhou, Ludu saw from afar their commander—man and horse both clad in gold—moving in and out of the battle line at a distance of about two hundred-odd paces; with one shot he struck the throat and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut attacked Huizhou, Ludu saw their commander from afar—man and horse both clad in gold—moving in and out of the battle line at a distance of some two hundred paces. With one shot he struck the man's throat and killed him.

sentences.zh: 又射一人，矢貫兩手於樹，敵大駭。

translations.literal: He shot another man as well; the arrow pierced both hands and pinned them to a tree, and the enemy were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: He shot another man as well, pinning both his hands to a tree with a single arrow. The enemy were terrified.

sentences.zh: 城破，祿大、蝦蟆俱被禽。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Ludu and Xiama were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, both Ludu and Xiama were captured.

sentences.zh: 夏人憐其技，囚之，兄弟皆誓死不屈。

translations.literal: The Tangut pitied their skill and imprisoned them; the brothers both vowed to die rather than submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut admired their skill and imprisoned them. Both brothers swore they would die rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，議加優獎，而未知存沒，乃特遷祿大子伴牛官一階，授巡尉職，以旌其忠。

translations.literal: The court heard of it and deliberated granting special rewards, but not knowing whether they lived or died, specially promoted Ludu's son Ban Niuguan one rank and appointed him to a patrol commander's post to honor their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of this, it planned special rewards, but not knowing whether the brothers were alive or dead, it specially promoted Ludu's son Ban Niuguan one rank and appointed him a patrol commander to honor their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其後兄弟謀奔會，自拔其須，事覺，祿大竟為所殺，蝦蟆獨拔歸。

translations.literal: Afterward the brothers plotted to flee back to Huizhou; they plucked out their own beards, but the matter was discovered. Ludu was ultimately killed by them, while Xiama alone broke free and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later the brothers plotted to escape back to Huizhou and plucked out their own beards to disguise themselves, but the plot was discovered. Ludu was killed, while Xiama alone broke free and made it back.

sentences.zh: 上思祿大之忠，命複遷伴牛官一階，遙授會州軍事判官，蝦蟆遙授鞏州鈐轄。

translations.literal: The emperor, remembering Ludu's loyalty, ordered Ban Niuguan promoted one rank again and Ludu given an honorary appointment as military adjutant of Huizhou; Xiama was given an honorary appointment as commandant of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering Ludu's loyalty, promoted Ban Niuguan one rank again and gave Ludu an honorary appointment as military adjutant of Huizhou. Xiama received an honorary appointment as commandant of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 會言者乞獎用祿大弟，遂遷蝦蟆官兩階，授同知蘭州軍州事。

translations.literal: At the time memorializers requested reward and employment for Ludu's younger brother; Xiama was therefore promoted two ranks and appointed acting co-administrator of Lanzhou prefecture and army.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists then asked that Ludu's younger brother be rewarded and employed. Xiama was promoted two ranks and appointed acting co-administrator of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 興定五年冬，夏人萬餘侵定西，蝦蟆敗之，斬首七百，獲馬五十匹，以功遷同知臨洮府事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Xingding, more than ten thousand Tangut invaded Dingxi; Xiama defeated them, beheaded seven hundred, captured fifty horses, and for merit was transferred to acting co-administrator of Lintao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year of Xingding, more than ten thousand Tangut invaded Dingxi. Xiama routed them, beheaded seven hundred men, and captured fifty horses. For this he was promoted to acting co-administrator of Lintao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元光二年，夏人步騎數十萬攻鳳翔甚急，元帥赤盞合喜以蝦蟆總領軍事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanguang, Tangut infantry and cavalry numbering several hundred thousand attacked Fengxiang with great urgency; Marshal Chizan Hexi put Xiama in overall charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanguang, several hundred thousand Tangut infantry and cavalry pressed the attack on Fengxiang. Marshal Chizan Hexi put Xiama in overall charge of the defense.

sentences.zh: 從巡城，濠外一人坐胡床，以箭力不及，氣貌若蔑視城守者。

translations.literal: Accompanying him on a circuit of the walls, outside the moat one man sat on a folding camp chair; judging the arrow's force could not reach, his bearing seemed to scorn the city's defenders.
translations.idiomatic: While making the rounds of the walls with him, they saw a man outside the moat seated on a folding camp chair. He seemed to think himself out of bowshot, and his manner looked contemptuous of the defenders.

sentences.zh: 合喜指似蝦蟆雲：「汝能射此人否？」

translations.literal: Hexi pointed him out to Xiama and said, "Can you shoot this man?"
translations.idiomatic: Hexi pointed the man out to Xiama and asked, "Can you hit him?"

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆測量遠近，曰：「可。」

translations.literal: Xiama measured the distance and said, "I can."
translations.idiomatic: Xiama gauged the distance and said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆平時發矢，伺腋下甲不掩處射之無不中，即持弓矢伺坐者舉肘，一發而斃。

translations.literal: In his usual shooting Xiama waited for places where armor under the armpit did not cover and shot there without ever missing; now he took bow and arrow, waited for the seated man to raise his elbow, and with one shot killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiama's usual method was to wait for gaps in the armor under the armpit; he never missed. He nocked an arrow, waited for the seated man to raise his elbow, and dropped him with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 兵退，升遙授靜難軍節度使，尋改通遠軍節度使，授山東西路斡可必剌謀克，仍遣使賞賚，遍諭諸郡焉。

translations.literal: The enemy withdrew; he was promoted to honorary Jingnan Army commissioner, soon changed to Tongyuan Army commissioner, appointed commander of the Shandong and Shaanxi Circuit's Wokebila regiment, and envoys were still sent with rewards and gifts, proclaiming this in all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew. He was promoted to honorary commissioner of the Jingnan Army, then reassigned as commissioner of the Tongyuan Army and appointed commander of the Wokebila regiment on the Shandong and Shaanxi Circuit. Envoys were sent with rewards, and the news was proclaimed in every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，蝦蟆與鞏州元帥田瑞攻取會州。

translations.literal: That winter Xiama and Gongzhou Marshal Tian Rui attacked and recovered Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xiama joined Gongzhou Marshal Tian Rui in attacking and retaking Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆率騎兵五百皆被赭衲，蔽州之南山而下，夏人猝望之以為神。

translations.literal: Xiama led five hundred cavalry all clad in ochre robes, descending concealed by the south mountain of the prefecture; the Tangut suddenly saw them and took them for gods.
translations.idiomatic: Xiama led five hundred cavalry clad in ochre robes, descending from behind the mountain south of the prefecture. The Tangut caught sight of them suddenly and thought they were divine beings.

sentences.zh: 城上有舉手於懸風版者，蝦蟆射之，手與版俱貫。

translations.literal: On the wall someone raised a hand above the wind-screen board; Xiama shot him, and hand and board were both pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: On the wall a man raised his hand above the parapet wind-screen. Xiama shot him, driving the arrow through both hand and screen.

sentences.zh: 凡射死數百人。

translations.literal: In all he shot dead several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: In all he killed several hundred men with his bow.

sentences.zh: 夏人震恐，乃出降。

translations.literal: The Tangut were shaken with terror and then came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the Tangut surrendered.

sentences.zh: 蓋會州為夏人所據近四年，至是複焉。

translations.literal: Huizhou had been held by the Tangut for nearly four years; at this time it was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou had been in Tangut hands for nearly four years; now it was recovered.

sentences.zh: 正大初，田瑞據鞏州叛，詔陝西兩行省並力擊之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengda, Tian Rui held Gongzhou and rebelled; an edict ordered the two Shaanxi branch secretariats to join forces and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengda era, Tian Rui seized Gongzhou and rebelled. An edict ordered the two Shaanxi branch secretariats to join forces and attack him.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆率眾先登，瑞開門突出，為其弟濟所殺，斬首五千餘級，以功遷遙授知鳳翔府事、本路兵馬都總管、元帥左都監、兼行蘭、會、洮、河元帥府事。

translations.literal: Xiama led the troops in scaling the walls first; Rui opened the gate and burst out, was killed by his younger brother Ji, and more than five thousand heads were cut off. For merit he was transferred to honorary administrator of Fengxiang Prefecture, overall commander of the circuit's military forces, left overseer of the marshal's staff, and concurrent acting marshal of the Lan, Hui, Tao, and He command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiama led the assault and was first over the wall. Rui opened the gate and charged out but was killed by his younger brother Ji. More than five thousand heads were taken. For this Xiama was promoted to honorary administrator of Fengxiang Prefecture, overall commander of the circuit's forces, left overseer of the marshal's staff, and acting marshal of the Lan, Hui, Tao, and He command.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，蝦蟆進西馬二匹，詔曰：「卿武藝超絕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year, Xiama presented two Western horses; an edict said, "Your martial skill is surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year, Xiama presented two Western horses. An edict said, "Your martial skill is extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 此馬可充戰用，朕乘此豈能盡其力。

translations.literal: These horses can serve in battle; if I ride them, how could I fully use their strength?
translations.idiomatic: These horses are fit for war. If I rode them, I could not make full use of their power.

sentences.zh: 既入進，即尚廄物也，就以賜卿。」

translations.literal: Once presented as tribute, they become imperial stable property; I therefore bestow them upon you."
translations.idiomatic: Once offered in tribute they belong to the imperial stables—so I bestow them upon you instead."

sentences.zh: 仍賜金鼎一、玉兔鶻一，並所遣郭倫哥等物有差。

translations.literal: He further bestowed one gold cauldron and one jade hunting hawk, and the goods sent with Guo Lunge and others were also graded in reward.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted a gold cauldron and a jade hunting hawk, along with graded rewards for Guo Lunge and the others who had accompanied the tribute.

sentences.zh: 天興二年，哀宗遷蔡州，慮孤城不能保，擬遷鞏昌，以粘葛完展為鞏昌行省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxing, Emperor Aizong moved to Caizhou; fearing the isolated city could not be held, he planned to move to Gongchang and appointed Niange Wanzhan as Gongchang branch secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxing, Emperor Aizong moved the court to Caizhou. Fearing the isolated city could not be held, he planned to relocate to Gongchang and appointed Niange Wanzhan branch secretary there.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，完展聞蔡已破，欲安眾心，城守以待嗣立者，乃遣人稱使者至自蔡，有旨宣諭。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year, Wanzhan heard that Cai had already fallen; wishing to settle the people's hearts, he held the city and waited for a successor to be enthroned. He then sent men posing as envoys arriving from Cai, bearing an edict to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the third year, Wanzhan learned that Cai had fallen. Hoping to steady morale, he held the city and waited for a successor to be enthroned. He sent men posing as envoys from Cai bearing an edict of instruction.

sentences.zh: 綏德州帥汪世顯者亦知蔡凶問，且嫉完展制己，欲發矯詔事，因以兵圖之，然懼蝦蟆威望，乃遣使約蝦蟆並力破鞏昌。

translations.literal: Suide Prefecture commander Wang Shixian also knew the grim news from Cai and resented Wanzhan's control over him; he wished to expose the forged edict affair and therefore plotted against him with troops, yet feared Xiama's prestige and so sent envoys to invite Xiama to join forces in breaking Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixian, commander of Suide Prefecture, also heard the grim news from Cai and resented Wanzhan's authority over him. He wanted to expose the forged edict and moved against Wanzhan with troops, but feared Xiama's prestige and sent envoys asking Xiama to join him in taking Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 使者至，蝦蟆謂之曰：「粘葛公奉詔為行省，號令孰敢不從。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, Xiama said to them, "Lord Niange was appointed branch secretary by imperial edict—whose orders would anyone dare not obey?
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived, Xiama told them, "Lord Niange holds his post by imperial edict. Whose orders would anyone dare disobey?

sentences.zh: 今主上受圍于蔡，擬遷鞏昌。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign is besieged at Cai and plans to move to Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is now besieged at Cai and plans to relocate to Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 國家危急之際，我輩既不能致死赴援，又不能葉眾奉迎，乃欲攻粘葛公，先廢遷幸之地，上至何所歸乎。

translations.literal: At a moment when the state is in peril, we can neither give our lives to go to the rescue nor abandon the multitude to welcome the sovereign—yet you wish to attack Lord Niange and first destroy the place chosen for the move. Where then would the sovereign go?
translations.idiomatic: At a moment when the state is in peril, we can neither give our lives to march to the rescue nor abandon the people here to welcome the sovereign—yet you would attack Lord Niange and destroy the very place chosen for the court's relocation. Where would the sovereign go then?

sentences.zh: 汝帥若欲背國家，任自為之，何及於我。」

translations.literal: If your commander wishes to betray the state, let him do as he pleases—what has that to do with me?"
translations.idiomatic: If your commander wishes to betray the state, let him do as he pleases. What has that to do with me?"

sentences.zh: 世顯即攻鞏昌破之，劫殺完展，送款於大元，複遣使者二十余輩諭蝦蟆以禍福，不從。

translations.literal: Shixian at once attacked Gongchang, broke it, seized and killed Wanzhan, submitted to the Great Yuan, and again sent more than twenty envoys to instruct Xiama on fortune and calamity, but he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian immediately attacked Gongchang, captured it, seized and killed Wanzhan, and submitted to the Yuan. He then sent more than twenty envoys to lecture Xiama on fortune and ruin, but Xiama refused.

sentences.zh: 甲午春，金國已亡，西州無不歸順者，獨蝦蟆堅守孤城。

translations.literal: In spring of the jiawu year the Jin state had perished; in the western prefectures none failed to submit—only Xiama held fast to his isolated city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the jiawu year the Jin state had fallen. Every western prefecture submitted—only Xiama continued to hold his isolated city.

sentences.zh: 丙申歲冬十月，大兵並力攻之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the bingshen year the main army attacked it with combined force.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the bingshen year the main army attacked the city with all its strength.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆度不能支，集州中所有金銀銅鐵，雜鑄為砲以擊攻者，殺牛馬以食戰士，又自焚盧舍積聚，曰：「無至資兵。」

translations.literal: Xiama judged he could not hold out, gathered all gold, silver, copper, and iron in the prefecture, cast them together into cannon to strike the attackers, slaughtered oxen and horses to feed the warriors, and burned his own dwellings and stores, saying: "Let nothing reach the enemy army."
translations.idiomatic: Xiama saw he could not hold out. He gathered every scrap of gold, silver, copper, and iron in the prefecture and cast them into cannon to strike the attackers. He slaughtered oxen and horses to feed his warriors and burned his own dwellings and stores, saying, "Let nothing fall into the enemy's hands."

sentences.zh: 日與血戰，而大兵亦不能卒拔。

translations.literal: Day by day they fought in blood, yet the main army also could not take it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day they fought bloody engagements, yet the main army could not capture the city quickly either.

sentences.zh: 及軍士死傷者眾，乃命積薪於州廨，呼集家人及城中將校妻女，閉諸一室，將自焚之。

translations.literal: When many soldiers had been killed or wounded, he ordered firewood piled at the prefectural offices, summoned his family and the wives and daughters of officers in the city, shut them in one room, and was about to burn them.
translations.idiomatic: When casualties among his troops had grown heavy, he ordered firewood piled in the prefectural offices, gathered his family and the wives and daughters of the city's officers, shut them in one room, and prepared to burn them alive.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆之妾欲有所訴，立斬以徇。

translations.literal: Xiama's concubine wished to plead; he beheaded her at once as an example.
translations.idiomatic: When one of Xiama's concubines tried to plead, he beheaded her on the spot as an example to the rest.

sentences.zh: 火既熾，率將士於火前持滿以待。

translations.literal: When the fire blazed up, he led his officers and men before it with bows drawn full to wait.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire was blazing, he led his officers and men to stand before it with bows drawn full, waiting.

sentences.zh: 城破，兵填委以入，鏖戰既久，士卒有弓盡矢絕者，挺身入火中。

translations.literal: When the city fell, troops poured in; after long fierce fighting, soldiers whose bows were spent and arrows exhausted threw themselves into the fire.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, enemy troops poured in. After prolonged fierce fighting, soldiers whose bows were broken and arrows spent threw themselves into the flames.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆獨上大草積，以門扉自蔽，發二三百矢無不中者，矢盡，投弓劍於火自焚。

translations.literal: Xiama alone climbed a great haystack, shielded himself with a door panel, loosed two or three hundred arrows without missing, and when arrows were spent cast bow and sword into the fire and burned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiama alone climbed a great haystack, shielded himself with a door panel, and loosed two or three hundred arrows without a miss. When his arrows were spent he cast his bow and sword into the fire and burned himself.

sentences.zh: 城中無一人肯降者。

translations.literal: In the city not one person was willing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Not a single person in the city was willing to surrender.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆死時年四十五。

translations.literal: When Xiama died he was forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Xiama was forty-five when he died.

sentences.zh: 土人為立祠。

translations.literal: The local people built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: The local people built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 完展字世昌。

translations.literal: Wanzhan's courtesy name was Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhan's courtesy name was Shichang.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年策論進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in policy essays in the third year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in policy essays in Taihe 3.

sentences.zh: 初為行省，以蠟丸為詔，期以天興二年九月集大軍與上會于饒峰關，出宋不意取興元。

translations.literal: When he first served as branch secretary, he used a wax pellet as an edict, fixing the ninth month of the second year of Tianxing to gather a great army and meet the sovereign at Raofeng Pass, taking Xingyuan when the Song did not expect it.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as branch secretary, he sent a wax-sealed edict fixing the ninth month of Tianxing 2 for a great army to rendezvous with the emperor at Raofeng Pass and seize Xingyuan before the Song could react.

sentences.zh: 既而不果雲。

translations.literal: In the end it did not succeed, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the plan came to nothing, or so it is said.
